short_name: INRAE (ANR) Infrastructure to boost the use of diversified biological resources (BreIF)
full_name: INRAE (ANR) Infrastructure to boost the use of diversified biological resources (BreIF)
summary:
The BReIF (Biological Resources Information Facility) project, funded by ANR and led by INRAE, develops a national e-infrastructure to accelerate the use of diversified biological resources for agroecological innovation. It addresses a major bottleneck in agricultural research: the integration and exploitation of large, heterogeneous datasets generated from the characterization of plant, animal, and microbial genetic resources. 
BReIF connects key French infrastructures (RARe, IFB, and France Génomique) to provide FAIR-compliant data management, interoperable tools, and a sustainable data portal. The project delivers reproducible genomic analysis pipelines, including genome assembly and pangenome analysis, alongside shared standards, best practices, and training. 
By enabling efficient data sharing, integration, and analysis, BReIF enhances the capacity to mobilize biodiversity for research and innovation, supporting resilient agricultural systems and contributing to climate-smart and sustainable food production.

short_name: University of Cambridge(The Mastercard Foundation)-Investigating smallholder banana planting material movement in East and West Africa
full_name: University of Cambridge(The Mastercard Foundation)-Investigating smallholder banana planting material movement in East and West Africa
summary:
This project investigates how smallholder banana planting material movement drives the spread of Banana Bunchy Top Disease (BBTD) across East and West Africa. Focusing on Rwanda, Benin, and Ghana, the study combines field data on farmer seed sourcing practices with spatial epidemiological modelling to identify risk pathways and hotspots for disease transmission. Particular attention is given to informal seed systems, cross-border exchanges, and contrasting production systems (highland banana vs. lowland plantain).

The project strengthens climate-resilient seed systems by generating evidence to guide clean seed dissemination and targeted disease management strategies. Outputs will support policymakers and partners in reducing BBTD risk, safeguarding banana production, and improving smallholder livelihoods.

By enhancing knowledge on the supply, access, and use of virus-free planting material, the initiative contributes to sustainable intensification and food security under climate change, while building regional capacity for data-driven disease surveillance and management.

The agenda also highlights the role of agrobiodiversity in delivering ecosystem services through multifunctional landscapes that support sustainability, prosperity, and resilience. short_name: FAO- Catalyzing momentum: fast-tracking the Biodiversity for Food and Nutrition Initiative ahead of COP17
full_name: FAO- Catalyzing momentum: fast-tracking the Biodiversity for Food and Nutrition Initiative ahead of COP17
summary: This project aims to support the CBD Member States in integrating biodiversity, nutrition, and sustainable food system considerations into National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs) and related agrifood policies. Building on the CBD’s Cross-cutting Initiative on Biodiversity for Food and Nutrition, the project will identify and document practical, country-driven entry points that strengthen the linkages between biodiversity conservation, healthy diets, and resilient agrifood systems. The initiative responds to increasing global challenges related to biodiversity loss, climate change, food insecurity, and malnutrition by promoting policies that deliver co-benefits for human and planetary health. Expected outcomes include the development of actionable guidance and tools for governments, strengthened integration of food biodiversity into biodiversity and agrifood system policies, increased public awareness of biodiversity–nutrition linkages, and enhanced support for the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. Project findings and recommendations will contribute to global policy discussions at CBD COP17 in 2026.

short_name: INDONESIA-BRIN (BMGF)- Cryopreservation of various vegetative and reproductive organs and callus of wild bananas
full_name: INDONESIA-BRIN (BMGF)- Cryopreservation of various vegetative and reproductive organs and callus of wild bananas
summary:
This 5 year project strengthens the safe conservation of banana genetic resources by building capacity, infrastructure, and validated protocols in partnership with Indonesian researchers (BRIN).
Early phases focus on hands on training in Leuven and Indonesia, optimizing cryopreservation of clonal materials and pollen, and supporting installation of operational cryo facilities. Subsequent years emphasize scaling up, including management of cryobanks, routine application of protocols, and sustained technical backstopping. Throughout, Indonesian partners progressively lead experimental work, supported by targeted expert input and exchanges. The project delivers practical guidelines and multiple peer reviewed publications, ensuring global relevance and uptake. Annual reporting and a final report guarantee accountability. 
Overall, the initiative creates durable in country capacity to conserve wild and improved banana diversity, directly contributing to resilient breeding systems and long term food security.

description:
The BREL project enhances forest restoration in Kalimantan by increasing the use of under-utilised tree species through innovative research, stakeholder engagement, and digital planning and monitoring tools, enhancing biodiversity, climate resilience, and community livelihoods. Using a multi-disciplinary approach, we will produce novel protocols to optimise restoration outcomes through selection of resilient plant communities which will support climate change mitigation and suit local socio-ecological contexts across lowland forests of Kalimantan. 

Species choices in existing restoration efforts have not been systematically documented and compared to the known native species diversity to assess gaps, and understanding of the current and potential species’ functional traits and resilience under future climates remains unknown. There is also a lack of knowledge on how under-utilised species can promote sustainable livelihoods as part of restoration activity through facilitating access to species with trade and utility value. This hampers further development of a bespoke and diverse species pool for use in Kalimantan lowland forests. There is introduced legislation to support the production and use of quality planting material in forest restoration, but implementation remains focused on a limited number of tree species.

The project will: 
(1) Publish a policy brief identifying key gaps in tree diversity (species, functional, economic) used in restoration and agroforestry when compared to the native tree flora, and analysing their impact on productivity and resilience in Kalimantan.
(2) Create new knowledge of species-site matching for diverse landscape contexts and land use objectives in a changing climate, released in the Diversity for Restoration tool with bespoke content for Kalimantan.
(3) Release the MyFarmTree app for Kalimantan to address bottlenecks in incorporating under-utilized species into seed and seedling supply chains and streamline the adoption of innovations in germplasm supply.
(4) Validate rapid/remote surveys for plant biodiversity metrics, to achieve efficient plant biodiversity monitoring methodology and demonstrate route to full Biodiversity Credit Certification for a selected site as a pilot.
(5) Disseminate decision support tools and new knowledge resources to enhance plant biodiversity in restoration efforts across Kalimantan, and link to existing seed supply chain infrastructure.
(6) Create new partnerships and joint infrastructure established for long-term enhancement and monitoring of plant biodiversity in restoration and associated livelihood benefits.

UNEP, UNDP and the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT implement the project in collaboration with the CBD Secretariat. The project objectives are:

1. Enhance institutional capacity: build technical and institutional capacity on gender equality and systems thinking through a core country team (CCT) in each partner country, integrating gender-responsive approaches into biodiversity policies and practices.
2. Increase women's participation and leadership through multi-stakeholder workshops and co-created, country-specific gender-responsive biodiversity solutions, linked to technical support and financing via the NBSAP Accelerator Partnership's MatchMaking Mechanism.

summary:

Preferred and well-adapted varieties will be identified through participatory selection processes and subsequently multiplied and disseminated among farming communities.
A comprehensive training programme will strengthen farmers' capacities in quality seed production, the implementation of PPVS, and the establishment and management of community seed banks. These activities will contribute to enhancing local seed availability and the resilience of farming systems. The active involvement of extension services will further support the functioning, recognition, and understanding of informal seed systems, fostering stronger linkages between farming communities and institutional actors while promoting the sustainable management and dissemination of plant genetic resources.

full_name: UNEP-Methane emissions baseline for livestock systems in Colombia (IA Lead of S294)
summary: This project will develop a national methane emissions baseline for livestock systems in Colombia to support evidence-based climate action and methane mitigation planning. The work will identify emissions hotspots across key livestock production systems and conduct direct methane measurements using polytunnel methodologies to generate robust field data. These measurements will improve understanding of emissions sources and provide a stronger scientific basis for estimating methane emissions at national scale. The project will also assess and compare mitigation options suitable for different production contexts, evaluating their potential effectiveness and feasibility. Results will be delivered to relevant government agencies to support policy development, climate reporting, and implementation of methane reduction strategies aligned with Colombia’s climate commitments and sustainable livestock development goals.

description: Challenges like biodiversity loss, soil erosion, unsecure land ownership, small farms, adverse climate change effects are impacting food and nutrition security in Vihiga. Since 2016, the Alliance's promotes community-based interventions to diversify farming systems and diets. This led to the established Community Seed Bank (CSB), covering 4 out of 5 sub-counties with aembership of about 300 farmers. While the positive results prompted the prioritization of an agroecological agenda at County level in 2022, the CSB is facing the twofold challenge of increasing its representation across the 5 sub-counties and improve seed documentation and characterization. To capitalize on these opportunities, the project fosters agroecological transitions in Vihiga towards an inclusive, healthy and resilient food system. Firstly, we scientifically characterize the diversity of seeds/planting materials in the CSB, allowing greater knowledge, use and conservation of local species (outcome 1). Secondly, we integrate native trees in the CSB portfolio, to further diversify farms and diets (outcome 2). Third, we work with local NGOs to expand the CSB membership at county level to transform it in a model resource centre, knowledge hub on AE and healthy diets and a platform for nature-based business development (outcome 3). short_name: Belgium-DGDC-Transforming agrifood systems in the Great Lakes region: incorporating agroecological solutions into banana production landscapes to boost climate resilience and reduce poverty
full_name: Belgium-DGDC-Transforming agrifood systems in the Great Lakes region: incorporating agroecological solutions into banana production landscapes to boost climate resilience and reduce poverty
summary:
Banana is central to food security and rural livelihoods in the African Great Lakes region but faces growing threats from climate change, soil degradation, and pests and diseases. This four-year project (2025–2028), led by the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT with regional partners, aims to transform banana systems through agroecological approaches and climate-smart, nutrient-efficient varieties.
Building on prior work, the project advances promising germplasm from the ITC gene bank, including varieties already tested in Uganda and Tanzania through field and farmer-led evaluations. The new phase integrates agroecological management with a focus on key traits such as nitrogen use efficiency and biological nitrification inhibition to reduce fertilizer dependence.
Combining laboratory screening, field validation, and participatory trials (TRICOT), the project strengthens national research capacity and seed systems. It supports resilient, low-input production, contributing to sustainable food systems, environmental restoration, and improved livelihoods.

full_name: EC Combating malnutrition in Africa through Diversification of the Food system (HealthyDiets4Africa)
summary: The project contributes to better informed nutrition policies that can be scaled-up by initiatives such as SUN (scaling-up nutrition) and UNFSS (United Food Systems Summit) post-processes via the following outputs: (i) Understanding of dietary habits across sub-Saharan Africa and intervention effects on dietary diversity; (ii) Novel and simple a priori indices that reflect total dietary diversity, quality for resource-poor settings developed and food environment risk factors for malnutrition; (iii) Identification of gender and nutritional health sensitive food environment indicators and metrics associated with malnutrition among different societal groups. Moreover, the project results contribute to improved nutrition in African countries reducing all forms of malnutrition through safe, healthy and affordable diets, including dietary shifts that reduce the pressure of food production on land and water use, and reduces the climate footprint. Outputs contributing to this aim include: (i) A database of vitamins, microelement contents and glycaemic value of traditional landraces, wild species, and breeding materials generated. (ii) Methods to increase the productivity and sustainability of diversified healthy foods documented; (iii) Policy debates, policies briefs, advocacy and communication tools that favor accessibility, affordability and sustainability of healthy food production and consumption elaborated and tested.
description: Both description and project summary filled. Various forms of malnutrition, including hunger, micronutrient deficiencies and non-communicable diseases caused by unbalanced nutrition, threaten food security in Africa. The project HealthyDiest4Africa is based on the central hypothesis that diversification of the food system helps to combat all forms of malnutrition while minimizing its environmental footprint. To this aim, we monitor dietary diversity in eight African countries representing different regions, and develop target group-specific metrics to measure the diversity of the food system and its health outcomes. A production-oriented cluster of the project explore environmentally sustainable options to diversity food production that specifically address the nutritional requirements identified for the target populations. This includes the development of novel and biofortified crop varieties, utilization of orphan crops with high nutritional value, and diversification of cropping systems and food processing technology. We link these efforts with a consumption-oriented cluster exploring the consumer acceptance, food safety, and nutritional health effects of diet diversification options. The best solutions that contribute to healthy diets via diversification while also promoting environmental health will be up-scaled via a network of food system stakeholders in eight African countries. HealthyDiets4Africa also devise communication and policy strategies to maximize outreach and impact of diversified food systems. Thereby the project help to develop safe, healthy and affordable diets by adopting a diversification strategy that simultaneously reduce the pressure of food production on the environment

short_name: Biovision-Enhancing Kenya’s Organic Food System through Improved Market Access for Vulnerable Consumers in Nairobi and Small-scale Farmers in Makueni County(Urban Nutrition Phase II)
full_name: Biovision-Enhancing Kenya’s Organic Food System through Improved Market Access for Vulnerable Consumers in Nairobi and Small-scale Farmers in Makueni County(Urban Nutrition Phase II)
summary: This project contributes to the development of a safe, inclusive, and regenerative food system in Kenya by strengthening organic fruit and vegetable value chains for smallholder farmers and vulnerable urban consumers. The initiative expects to improve livelihoods of farmers in Makueni County through the adoption of regenerative and agroecological farming practices, establishment of community seedbanks, strengthened water management systems, and formation of farmer cooperatives. The project will also enhance market access through participatory organic certification systems, creation of community-led markets, and development of innovative business models linking producers and consumers in Makueni and Nairobi. Additionally, it aims to increase awareness and consumption of healthy diets among rural and urban households through nutrition education, school engagement, urban demonstration gardens, and digital outreach. Finally, the project will strengthen the science-policy interface by generating evidence, policy briefs, and stakeholder engagement processes to support equitable, sustainable, and health-oriented food system transformation in Kenya.

short_name: UNITED KINGDOM - FCDO -iSPARK: Innovation in sustainability, policy, adaptation and resilience in Kenya (IA Lead of D511)
full_name: UNITED KINGDOM - FCDO -iSPARK: Innovation in sustainability, policy, adaptation and resilience in Kenya (IA Lead of D511)
summary: In Kenya, environmental degradation and climate change threaten the sustainability and resilience of smallholder farming systems. Farmers need timely and accurate climate information combined with agro-advisories to make informed decisions. Meanwhile, policy makers need evidence to prioritize policy choices and investment decisions that contribute to environmental sustainability, climate resilience, and other development goals by mid-century. iSPARK is designed to tailor evidence towards supporting appropriate and contextualised advisory services, policies, and investment in equity-sensitive sustainable and climate-smart innovation in western Kenya, building on CGIAR Initiatives on Climate Resilience and Excellence in Agronomy. The core of iSPARK is developing and using a metric-based approach called Innovation in Sustainability, Resilience, and Adaptation (ISRA) to provide specific evidence for innovations and pathways at different levels, from individual farms to regional policies. iSPARK aims to integrate ISRA metrics into agro-advisories reaching 100,000 farmers; create/support at least one plan/policy; and create/support at least one investment case or funding proposal by 2026.

short_name: IUCN (GEF)-Restoration Challenge Grant Platform for Smallholders and Communities, with Blockchain-Enabled Crowdfunding
full_name: IUCN (GEF)-Restoration Challenge Grant Platform for Smallholders and Communities, with Blockchain-Enabled Crowdfunding
summary: Project Objective: To facilitate, support, and mobilize investment in, smallholder and community-led restoration of critical landscapes to provide global environmental benefits and enhanced resilient economic development and livelihoods, in support of the Bonn Challenge, AFR100, the Trillion Tree Campaign, and other global and national restoration efforts
description: Both description and summary filled. The Restoration Challenge Grant Platform for Smallholders and Communities, with Blockchain-Enabled Crowdfunding (hereafter referred to as the Platform), will facilitate and support enhanced smallholder and rural community member engagement and investment in restoration. The Platform will utilize mobile cellular technology and payment transfer services to provide small grants/payments for smallholder-, community-, and school-led restoration work ‚Äì principally tree-planting ‚Äì matched by co-investment (in-kind and/or cash). Cellular technology will allow for efficient and effective verification of work and transfer of payments. Another key innovative focus of the Platform will be the integration of blockchain technology throughout the restoration value chain to provide transparency, build trust, facilitate real-time monitoring, evaluation and verification, and support mobilization of funding for restoration. From appropriate species selection, seed sourcing and seedling propagation, to tree planting and maintenance and transfer of payments, each transaction will be marked by a unique, traceable, unchangeable and verifiable blockchain. A second phase of the Platform will utilize a public-facing web platform and partnerships with other tree planting and restoration investment matching platforms to facilitate crowdfunding of Platform-supported restoration and financial sustainability, drawing upon the blockchain technology and ledger for security and transparency and trustworthyness of crowdfunded transactions. A range of engagement approaches and selection of a diverse group of landscapes will allow for cross comparison and learning to inform restoration initiatives going forward. Upon successful development and implementation of the Platform including blockchain-enabled crowdfunding, the Platform will function as a freestanding initiative ‚Äì one that can inform and link with other global and regional initiatives and platforms supporting the restoration agenda, including the Trillion Trees Initiative, UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration, and others.

short_name: GATES (Ex-BMGF)- CG partnerships: private sector investments in ag R&D
full_name: GATES (Ex-BMGF)- CG partnerships: private sector investments in ag R&D
summary:
AFII (Agri-Food Innovation Intelligence) is an AI-enabled global platform that maps and analyzes companies across agrifood value chains to help CGIAR, NARS, and other innovation actors identify the best private-sector partners for joint research, scaling, and resource mobilization.
It is essentially a “who is who” and “who does what” intelligence system for the global agrifood economy, combining structured firm data with AI-driven search and discovery tools. The core purpose of AFII is to make private-sector landscapes visible and usable for CGIAR and public agricultural research systems, enabling more strategic partnerships, better commercialization pathways, and stronger alignment between research outputs and market actors. By doing so, it helps accelerate the scaling of innovations and improves the effectiveness of public and private investment in agricultural development.
description:
AFII is a partner discovery and matchmaking tool designed to identify and connect innovative actors across agrifood value chains. It supports joint R&D, technology scaling, and resource mobilization by providing a structured overview of who is innovating, where, and with what capabilities.
The platform systematically maps private agrifood innovation actors and their attributes, using internationally recognized classifications. Users can explore this information through a digital interface, using both structured navigation (e.g. by crop, technology, or value chain segment) and AI-enabled free-text queries.
AFII enables users to:
•	Identify relevant innovation partners across value chains
•	Understand firm capabilities, activities, and market positioning
•	Explore innovation landscapes at national and regional levels
AFII is designed for a broad set of users, including public research organizations, private companies, industry associations, investors, and development partners. It supports decision-making related to:
•	Identifying which firms to engage for joint or complementary R&D, based on their technology focus, capabilities, and position in the value chain
•	Identifying firms that can realistically take innovations to scale, including firms with existing production, distribution, or market access
•	Assessing opportunities for licensing (in or out) technologies, based on which firms ares active in specific crops, technologies, or geographies
•	Targeting companies for collaboration or co-investment, where interests and capabilities align
•	Identifying gaps, overlaps, and missed linkages in the innovation system, including where public and private efforts are not well aligned

short_name: UGANDA - NARO  Novel approaches to the improvement of banana production in Eastern Africa: the application of biotechnological methodologies -- Phase IV
full_name: UGANDA - NARO  Novel approaches to the improvement of banana production in Eastern Africa: the application of biotechnological methodologies -- Phase IV
summary:
The project aims to increase the productivity of banana-based cropping systems in Uganda and strengthen the subsector’s contribution to agricultural GDP. This is being achieved through the development and dissemination of banana varieties resistant to key biotic stresses (pests and diseases) and abiotic stresses (drought and salinity), ensuring sustainable production and market responsiveness.
The project also builds national capacity by strengthening human resources and research infrastructure to support the deployment of advanced biotechnological tools. To date, significant progress has been made in developing resistance to weevils, nematodes, and Fusarium wilt in dessert and East African Highland bananas.
Now in Phase IV, the project focuses on investigating the release of pest-resistant varieties, developing new genetic solutions for Fusarium resistance, and strengthening genome editing capacity. Key activities include confined field trials, gene discovery, germplasm conservation in Mbarara, and the completion of a new biotech tissue culture laboratory.

full_name: ITALY–Italy Voluntary contribution 2024-Italian Support to Strategic Objectives (IA Lead of O159)
summary: The project funded by the Italian government to support the Alliance of Bioversity and CIAT’s strategic objectives aim to transform food systems in Africa through partnerships, diversification and policy leadership. The Regional East Africa Initiative supports Uganda, Ethiopia and Kenya by integrating coffee agroforestry with neglected and indigenous crops, strengthening inclusive markets, digital traceability, seed systems and regenerative farming. It seeks to improve food security, farmer incomes, biodiversity and climate resilience while reaching over 100,000 smallholders and influencing millions through policy reform. The Alliance of Champions for Food Systems Transformation is a country-led coalition that supports national food systems strategies, expands membership, mobilizes investment and advocates globally for resilient, sustainable agri-food systems by 2030. description:
The project funded by the Italian government to support the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT's strategic objectives is made up of three initiatives and a component for strategic engagement with Italy.

1.	Regional East Africa Initiative: diversified production and resilient market systems for coffee and opportunity crops
East Africa's food systems are at a critical juncture, challenged by intensifying climate shocks (erratic rainfall, prolonged droughts, and rising temperatures),  widespread soil erosion, nutrient depletion, biodiversity loss and unsustainable overreliance on a narrow set of staple crops. This vulnerability leaves millions of smallholders across the region exposed to food insecurity, hidden malnutrition, and economic precarity, even as the continent's extraordinary agrobiodiversity offers untapped solutions through Neglected and Underutilized Species (NUS), nutrient-dense African Indigenous Vegetables (AIVs), non-timber forest products (NTFPs) including wild fruits and medicinal plants, and the regenerative potential of shade-grown coffee agroforestry systems. This is where the Regional East Africa Initiative: Diversified Production & Resilient Market Systems for Coffee and Opportunity Crops begins - a strategic scaling of proven, successful initiatives and practices. It's a bold, multi-country Public-Private Partnership (PPP) uniting Uganda, Ethiopia, and Kenya in coordinated action on these intertwined crises. By focusing on these “forgotten crops” (long sidelined by research gaps, funding biases, and market neglect), the initiative pivots on two foundational pillars: production system diversification and inclusive market systems.   Production system diversification promotes strategic integration and systematic inclusion of NUS and AIV, through appropriate species selection, spacing and management,  in small-scale (coffee) farms, aggregated farms, and agroforestry systems   The implementation of an inclusive market system aims to reduce structural barriers like market fragmentation, price volatility, weak aggregation, finance droughts, and EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) compliance risks via digital traceability platforms, youth- and women-led aggregation hubs, and corridor-based demand consolidation linking rural producers to urban consumers, schools, processors, and export markets.
The initiative’s global objective is: to enhance East Africa's food security, farm resilience, and economic growth by strengthening sustainable, inclusive value chains for coffee, opportunity crops, and AIVs; more specifically: to enhance livelihoods of small-scale farmers through market inclusion and sustainable, diversified agricultural and agroforestry practices in Ethiopia, Kenya, and Uganda. At the regional level, the initiative fosters regional practice dissemination, policy dialogue, African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) linkages, and cross-country knowledge sharing, while country outcomes drive national impact: zero-deforestation coffee agroforestry systems in Ethiopia, boosted commercial activity along AIV/NUS corridors in Kenya, and scaled regenerative coffee-NUS/AIV agroforestry in Uganda.
Regionally, this manifests through an African Seed and Biotechnology Program (ASBP) regional policy workshops, evidence-based policy briefs, scaling support for regenerative agriculture based on diversification and inclusive market development, and CIHEAM Bari trainings equipping farmers, extensionists, and project staff with regenerative diversification skills.  Nationally, Ethiopia, - in collaboration with UNIDO and local partners such as cooperatives/unions (e.g. OFE/EFD/ECTA/NWRA), NABU, FARM Africa, TechnoServe, and private exporters - customizes digital advisory platforms like aCLIMAtar/D4A, rolls out EUDR traceability via TraceFoodChainTerra-i+ apps, establishes multi-stakeholder platforms, and co-designs inclusive business models. Through targeted capacity building activities, the initiative aims to reach 10,000 forest coffee smallholders, midstream traders/cooperatives, and forest communities; Kenya, in collaboration with ECDPM and strong local partnerships with,  Vihiga/Kisumu/Nakuru/Nairobi counties, AgriTech4Kenya startups, farmer cooperatives, vendor associations, youth facilitators and financial institutions - builds corridor platforms, strengthens community seedbanks and AIV farmer cooperatives, supports youth-led aggregation/logistics, fosters institutional buyer linkages and finance integration, targeting 7,000 AIV/NUS farmers, 400 value chain actors, and 40,000 urban consumers/institutions; Uganda, - in collaboration with UNIDO, private companies (such as Mountain Harvest (U) Ltd), cooperatives (e.g. MEACCE, MEHCS, Uganda Coffee Farmers alliance), and farmer networks (PELUM, NUCAFE, UCFA),  maps stakeholders and updates coffee typologies, co-designs NUS-tree agroforestry guidelines, incubates nature-based enterprises and business models, and scales best practices through Training of Trainers programs and living labs, impacting 100,000 coffee households, service providers, and policymakers .
Spearheaded by the Centre alongside UNIDO, CIHEAM Bari, ECDPM, national partners, farmer cooperatives, and private companies, the initiative delivers EUDR-compliant platforms, resilient seed systems, scalable diversification and market system innovations, GESI-embedded capacity building, policy tools, and A4IP’s acceleration and market integration models, reaching 100,000+ smallholders regionally via extension/ToT/cooperatives, 600 value chain operators, and a multitude of vulnerable consumers. The partnership with UNIDO will foster integration and replication of the project’s promising innovations within future programmes and investments. This has potential to further scale the scope of influence to at least 1,000,000 more smallholder farmers Policy scaling pathways (150+ policymakers to be engaged) can further enable indirect benefits for millions.
The promise is profound and measurable: boosts in yields, incomes, and dietary diversity; rehabilitated soils with enhanced carbon sequestration and water retention; biodiversity corridors via agroecological revival; reliable year-round nutrition for urban poor and school feeding; enhanced market systems and deforestation-free, traceable exports securing premium EU markets; and seamless alignment with continental frameworks like African Union Agenda 2063, Kampala Declaration (CAADP), post-Malabo commitments, Africa's Common Position on Food Systems, Italy's Mattei Plan (prioritizing climate-resilient coffee), and the EU Global Gateway strategy ultimately reimagining nature-positive, equitable livelihoods through revitalized value chains and inclusive, resilient food systems supporting regional economic growth.    
The component focuses on Uganda, Ethiopia and Kenya.

2.	Cacao Connect 
Cacao Connect brings together diplomacy, research, industry and civil society to support more sustainable, resilient and inclusive cocoa value chains across Africa. Led by MAECI, in collaboration with the Centre, Ferrero Group and Save the Children Italy, the Initiative connects origin-country priorities with Italian technical, scientific, industrial and financial expertise. The Alliance serves as the Initiative’s Knowledge Partner, ensuring technical coherence, evidence-based design, and alignment between country priorities, the Theory of Change and implementation pathways.  
The Initiative focuses on four origin countries: Ghana, Côte d’Ivoire, Guinea and Congo Brazzaville.

3.	The Alliance of Champions for Food Systems Transformation (ACF): delivering country-led change to 2030
The Alliance of Champions for Food Systems Transformation (ACF) is an established high-ambition, country-led coalition, driving whole-of-government action on food systems. This project seeks for the next 12-month implementation phase (June 2026 –May 2027), to consolidate ACF as a platform and accelerate progress toward its 2030 objectives. The ACF’s goals are three-fold: i) build momentum as an ambitious country-led alliance, growing to up to 15 members by 2030, with a strong and united North–South voice, and as a trusted platform for peer-to-peer learning; ii) support members to implement and deliver on food systems transformation, and iii) advance the food systems agenda globally by demonstrating visible and credible progress and using ACF members’ collective voice to advocate for action on resilient food systems in key multilateral fora. As one of the newest members of the Alliance, Italy brings critical political leadership and technical expertise, strengthening the ACF’s collective ambition and reinforcing its ability to deliver impact through to 2030. In turn, the ACF can offer Italy the opportunity to showcase its domestic progress and advance its foreign and development policy objectives on food systems, especially in Africa.
The ACF has three key goals to deliver real world outcomes to 2030, each with detailed objectives for Phase 1 (2026-2027). 
1.	Build momentum as an ambitious country-led alliance, growing to up to 15 members by 2030 – with a united North-South voice, and as a trusted platform for peer-to-peer learning. 
• Phase 1 objective: ACF membership expands to at least two more countries by March 2027, bringing the Alliance to a total of ten members, with scope to welcome a new African member as one of these two (potentially Tanzania, Senegal or Ethiopia). 
2. Support members’ delivery of food systems transformation, via support to i) implement key aspects of their national food systems plans, NDCs and NBSAPs and ii) where there is appetite, translate policy objectives into investable projects. 
• Phase 1 objectives: i. support integration of food systems transformation into key strategies, including those relating to biodiversity ahead of CBD COP17, and ii. enable 2-5 members to access key partnerships, tools and resources to deliver their national food systems transformation priorities. 
3. Advance the food systems agenda globally by i) demonstrating credible – and well publicised – member progress against core outcomes, ii) telling the ACF story clearly and iii) using the ACF’s voice to advocate for food systems transformation in multilateral fora. 
• Phase 1 objectives: 
i. Launch a comprehensive set of ‘progress frameworks’ and ‘snapshots’ -including for the ACF’s three newest members - at UNFCC COP31, to outline measurable progress against ACF’s ten priority action areas.
ii. Strengthen strategic communications capacity and build a recognised brand with traction. This will include placing 2-3 high-level op-eds in international and regional news outlets, and showcasing member success stories through media engagement and a growing ACF LinkedIn presence.
iii. Use the ACF’s collective voice to advocate for enhanced resilience across food systems, and improved volumes, quality and access of international finance for agri-food systems (including climate finance).

summary: This project develops a climate vulnerability assessment for Ahuachapán Sur, El Salvador, to strengthen understanding of climate risks affecting local livelihoods and agricultural systems. Through the integration of climate, environmental, and socioeconomic information, it identifies priority vulnerabilities and supports the development of evidence-based adaptation responses. The initiative engages local stakeholders in validating findings and strengthening their capacity to use climate risk information for planning and decision-making. By improving access to actionable evidence and supporting the identification of resilience-building measures, the project contributes to more informed local development processes, strengthened adaptive capacity, and enhanced preparedness for current and future climate challenges.

short_name: CICERO (RCN) - System adaptation for OneHealth under Climate change for Vulnerable groups and Ecosystems (SOLVE)
full_name: CICERO (RCN) - System adaptation for OneHealth under Climate change for Vulnerable groups and Ecosystems (SOLVE)
summary: The project aims to co-develop local adaptation roadmaps with societal partners to build resilient, healthy, equitable, and prosperous food and land systems. Using a suite of models, SOLVE integrates future climate extreme risks into long-term planning and promotes a OneHealth approach to better understand and address the complex interactions between people and nature. Taking the Omo-Ghibe basin as an implementation area, the project aims to account for stakeholder needs anf gaps, as well as integrate local knowledge to improve livelihoods and resilience, supporting food security and nutrition; guide regional and local agencies in developing effective climate adaptation strategies; provide data to support policies tailored to local needs and conditions; provide policy insights in support of sustainable use of water and land resources; inform focused interventions to strengthen community resilience and productivity.

short_name: GERMANY-GIZ (GERMANY-BMZ)-Climate Change Impacts on Deforestation and Crop Expansion in Cashew Growing Regions in Cote d’Ivoire and Ghana
full_name: GERMANY-GIZ (GERMANY-BMZ)-Climate Change Impacts on Deforestation and Crop Expansion in Cashew Growing Regions in Cote d’Ivoire and Ghana
summary: This project assesses how climate change is reshaping agricultural production landscapes in Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana, with a particular focus on cashew expansion and its implications for deforestation, biodiversity, and food production systems. Using climate suitability modelling, climate risk analysis, biodiversity assessments, and spatial overlay techniques, the study identifies areas where future agricultural expansion can occur sustainably and areas requiring conservation, restoration, or biodiversity buffer zones. The results will provide evidence-based guidance to support climate-resilient agricultural development while safeguarding ecosystems and reducing deforestation risks.
description: The project applies a landscape-level analytical framework to understand how climate change and climate extremes are shifting the suitability of cashew and other major cash and food crops across Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana. It combines climate suitability modelling, climate hazard assessment, tree species diversity modelling, and spatial analyses of land-use change, biodiversity, and deforestation risk. The study will quantify the implications of changing crop suitability on agricultural expansion, food-cash crop dynamics, and ecosystem integrity, while identifying climate vulnerability hotspots, biodiversity conservation priorities, restoration opportunities, and sustainable agricultural transition zones. The work is structured around five work packages covering stakeholder engagement, climate and risk analysis, crop suitability and tension analysis, biodiversity modelling, and integrated spatial overlay assessment

short_name: AGRA -PABRA 2023 Africa Food Prize
full_name: AGRA -PABRA 2023 Africa Food Prize
summary: The AGRA-PABRA 2023 Africa Food Prize record relates to institutional recognition and support associated with PABRA’s contribution to bean research, capacity strengthening, and delivery across Africa. The award recognizes PABRA’s role in establishing and coordinating a dynamic network of scientists, practitioners, and partners working to develop improved bean varieties and sustainable markets. Through this work, PABRA has contributed to food security, income generation, and improved nutrition for smallholder farmers and urban consumers. For mapping purposes, this record is most strongly aligned with capacity sharing, institutional strengthening, partnership coordination, and the scaling of bean research outcomes across African countries.

short_name: MARFRIG - Refining Tier 2 Emission Factors for Brazil and Support Marfrig’s Key Producing Countries with the Implementation of MRV of Emissions and Mitigation from Beef Cattle Suppliers
full_name: MARFRIG - Refining Tier 2 Emission Factors for Brazil and Support Marfrig’s Key Producing Countries with the Implementation of MRV of Emissions and Mitigation from Beef Cattle Suppliers
summary: Supporting Marfrig in improving greenhouse gas accounting and MRV systems across key beef-producing countries.
description: This project supports Marfrig in strengthening the scientific basis and credibility of its greenhouse gas accounting and mitigation strategies. Activities include refining Tier 2 enteric methane emission factors for Brazilian beef production systems, improving estimation methodologies, and supporting the implementation of MRV systems across major beef sourcing countries. The work evaluates mitigation opportunities, develops emissions baselines, and assesses pathways to achieve corporate climate targets aligned with international frameworks such as the GHG Protocol and SBTi FLAG. The project also helps improve data quality, transparency, and reporting consistency throughout Marfrig’s supply chain and sustainability programs.

short_name: COSTA RICA-CONARROZ-Desarrollar actividades conjuntas del Programa  Acelerado de Transferencia de TecnologIa y Aumento de Productividad del FLAR
full_name: COSTA RICA-CONARROZ-Desarrollar actividades conjuntas del Programa  Acelerado de Transferencia de TecnologIa y Aumento de Productividad del FLAR
summary: The project is a collaboration between CIAT, CONARROZ and SENUMISA to implement the Accelerated Technology Transfer Program for increasing FLAR rice productivity in Costa Rica. It seeks to strengthen the rice sector by validating, demonstrating and transferring improved agronomic practices and technologies that make rice production more efficient, profitable and sustainable. The project focuses on establishing FLAR demonstration plots, conducting technical visits by FLAR specialists, and providing in-person and virtual training and advisory services to technicians and producers. CIAT is responsible for technical guidance, protocols for plot management, monitoring, reports, and evaluation of agronomic performance, costs and results. CONARROZ supports local coordination, logistics, communication with producers, and follow-up through a technical committee, while SENUMISA contributes planning and field implementation. Overall, the initiative aims to build producer capacity, promote innovation, reduce production constraints, and support Costa Rica’s rice value chain with practical field-based evidence, knowledge transfer, and improved long-term sector competitiveness.

short_name: BID-Elaboración del Plan Nacional de Adaptación al Cambio Climático del Sector Agropecuario y Rural de Costa Rica (PASAR)
full_name: BID-Elaboración del Plan Nacional de Adaptación al Cambio Climático del Sector Agropecuario y Rural de Costa Rica (PASAR)
summary: This project supports the development of Costa Rica’s National Adaptation Plan for the Agricultural and Rural Sector through evidence generation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning. The initiative identifies adaptation priorities, enabling conditions, and institutional mechanisms required to strengthen resilience and competitiveness across the sector. Through collaboration with government agencies, producer organizations, and technical institutions, it promotes the integration of climate risk considerations into sectoral planning and decision-making processes. The project strengthens institutional capacities to design, implement, and monitor adaptation actions while incorporating gender, youth, Indigenous peoples, and vulnerable groups. By supporting evidence-based policy development, it contributes to more resilient, inclusive, and climate-informed agricultural and rural development pathways.

short_name: Nestlé - Adapt and optimize Croppie yield estimates for routine use in Nestlé’s breeding programs, validating its accuracy and efficiency
full_name: Nestlé - Adapt and optimize Croppie yield estimates for routine use in Nestlé’s breeding programs, validating its accuracy and efficiency
summary: Nestlé coffee breeding programs face challenges in scaling recurrent evaluations across large numbers of genotypes to identify promising materials. This project explores the use of automated image-based cherry counts to generate tree-level coffee yield predictions, with the aim of streamlining Nestlé’s breeding operations. It builds on Croppie, an existing tool developed by the Alliance. We will focus on model calibration and optimization of tree-level sampling intensity for both Arabica and Robusta. A cost-efficiency analysis will also be conducted to support Nestlé’s decision on whether and how to integrate the tool into its operations.

short_name: UNDP-Productos Climáticos
full_name: UNDP-Productos Climáticos
summary: This project supports the documentation, validation, and dissemination of climate-resilient agricultural practices and technologies in Ahuachapán, El Salvador. Through participatory processes involving producers, technical experts, and local institutions, it develops technology packages that consolidate local knowledge and practical experience into actionable guidance for farmers. The initiative strengthens local capacities, promotes knowledge sharing, and supports the broader adoption of resilient production practices adapted to local conditions. By generating accessible technical products and strengthening linkages among stakeholders, the project contributes to improved adaptive capacity, informed decision-making, and the replication of successful approaches that enhance resilience and sustainability within local agrifood systems.

short_name: WB-IBRD-Achieving livestock triple wins in  Brazil (CH4D)
full_name: WB-IBRD-Achieving livestock triple wins in  Brazil (CH4D)
summary: Assessing opportunities to achieve simultaneous climate, productivity, and livelihood benefits in Brazil’s livestock sector.
description: This project assesses pathways for achieving simultaneous climate, productivity, and livelihood benefits (“triple wins”) in Brazil’s livestock sector. Through detailed modeling of representative beef and dairy systems, the study evaluates how improved pasture management, animal performance, feed interventions, and other sustainable intensification practices affect greenhouse gas emissions, productivity, profitability, and resilience. The analysis identifies key mitigation opportunities, explores trade-offs between emission intensity and absolute emissions, and estimates scaling potential under different adoption scenarios. Findings are intended to inform public policy, investment strategies, and climate finance opportunities that can support sustainable livestock development in Brazil.

short_name: France-CIRAD-Evaluation of the use of genome editing for increasing the level of recombination in rice
full_name: France-CIRAD-Evaluation of the use of genome editing for increasing the level of recombination in rice
summary: This CIRAD-CIAT research and development contract evaluates the use of genome editing to increase recombination in rice as part of the PEPR Advanced Varietal Selection DivEdit project. The activity is applied biological research and will develop and evaluate edited rice lines in field conditions close to rice production environments. The work involves the Alliance genome editing platform and the rice improvement/biofortification team led by Jérôme Bartholomé. Expected outputs include five rice lines edited for the RECQ4 gene and phenotypic data for edited and non-edited populations. The project aligns directly with Breeding for Tomorrow because it develops advanced breeding methods, genomic tools and new knowledge to improve recombination, genetic diversity and future rice breeding efficiency.

short_name: GERMANY-GIZ-DIG-IN Honduras: DIGital INtegration of EUDR compliance Digital Public Infrastructures and financial sector systems in Honduras
full_name: GERMANY-GIZ-DIG-IN Honduras: DIGital INtegration of EUDR compliance Digital Public Infrastructures and financial sector systems in Honduras
summary:
The project aims to strengthen the inclusion of smallholder coffee producers in sustainable export markets by linking EUDR traceability data with financial sector risk assessment systems. The initiative seeks to reduce the risk of exclusion from European markets while addressing longstanding barriers to formal credit access faced by smallholder farmers in Honduras.
Through development of interoperable digital infrastructure, tailored financial products, and exporter validation processes, the project will enable traceability data to support regulatory compliance and informed lending decisions. Activities include designing farmer-centered credit products, integrating traceability and financial systems, validating compliance with EU due diligence requirements, and strengthening the capacities of farmers, cooperatives, exporters, and financial institutions.
Expected outcomes include increased access to affordable finance, improved EUDR compliance among smallholder producers, enhanced market access to the EU, stronger digital and financial inclusion, and greater participation of women and marginalized groups in sustainable coffee value chains.

short_name: Hershey - Identification of scalable soil health enhancing practices that improve the productivity and climate resilience of cocoa production systems.
full_name: Hershey - Identification of scalable soil health enhancing practices that improve the productivity and climate resilience of cocoa production systems.

Proposed activities focus on a combination of socio-economic feasibility assessment, on-farm agronomic field experiments, and development of sustainable business models and scaling pathways.

short_name: McKnight Foundation-Advancing Climate Data Integration in Agroecological Research
full_name: McKnight Foundation-Advancing Climate Data Integration in Agroecological Research
summary: This project develops an open-access climate data toolkit to enhance climate integration in agroecological research, targeting smallholder farming systems in the Andes, West Africa, and East and Southern Africa. Despite agroecology's potential as a climate solution, less than 25% of McKnight-funded projects explicitly incorporate climate analysis, partly due to the complexity of existing tools. The project co-creates user-friendly resources enabling researchers with limited climate science backgrounds to identify climate stresses, assess crop management options, and evaluate farming system resilience. Key deliverables include the climate toolkit, training materials, user engagement workshops with agroecological hubs, and a peer-reviewed publication synthesising evidence on agroecological practices for climate adaptation. The project collaborates with Stats4SD, IDEMS, and CGIAR partners.
description:
Climate change poses an urgent threat to smallholder food systems, yet less than a quarter of agroecological research projects explicitly connect their work to climate risk analysis. This disconnect limits the evidence base for agroecology as a climate solution and reduces the ability of researchers and policymakers to demonstrate impact. This project, funded by the McKnight Foundation's Collaborative Research for Resilient Food Systems (CRFs) programme under its thematic open call on agroecology as a bold climate solution, addresses this gap directly.
The Alliance of Bioversity-CIAT leads development of an open-access, modular climate data toolkit designed for researchers with minimal climate science backgrounds. The toolkit enables users to access and analyse climate data relevant to their study contexts, identify when climate stresses and shocks occur, and assess how different agroecological farming strategies affect system resilience. Tool development is co-designed with end users through a rapid user landscape assessment, structured interviews, user stories, and iterative feedback workshops, ensuring the toolkit reflects real researcher workflows and needs.
The project engages agroecological research hubs across the Andes, West Africa, and East and Southern Africa, as well as partners including Stats4SD, IDEMS, and relevant CGIAR bilateral projects. A case study using the ERA (Ecological Intensification) dataset grounds toolkit development in real agroecological data. Three training sessions with agroecological hubs are planned, alongside a peer-reviewed publication synthesising evidence on agroecological practices and climate adaptation outcomes.
Key outcomes include: (1) a validated, open-access climate data toolkit; (2) training resources and documentation; (3) a peer-reviewed publication; and (4) strengthened capacity among agroecological researchers to integrate climate data into their work and policy outputs, contributing to a stronger evidence base for agroecology as a climate adaptation strategy.

full_name: UNOPS - Monitoring and Evaluating Nature-based Solutions to Manage Kenya’s Biodiversity Hotspots using the Chyulu Hills as an Example

The initiative will develop a national NbS Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) framework  using the Chyulu Hills biodiversity hotspot as a pilot case study.  The project is expected to improve evidence-based decision-making, support reporting on Kenya’s climate commitments (NDCs, NCCAP, and BTRs), enhance ecosystem resilience and biodiversity conservation, and promote sustainable livelihoods for communities surrounding key biodiversity areas. short_name: PIN-People in Need-Leveraging and Expanding Agri-Aqua Production in Bangsamoro (LEAP), Philippines through climate services
full_name: PIN-People in Need-Leveraging and Expanding Agri-Aqua Production in Bangsamoro (LEAP), Philippines through climate services

Key outcomes include operational climate service products for coffee and seaweed, enhanced technical capacity among local institutions such as MAFAR, and formalized partnerships through MOUs — ensuring that climate services are institutionally embedded and sustained beyond the project period.

short_name: INDIA -TNAU (BMGF) Capacity Building on Cell Phone and Drone Data Collection and Processing
full_name: INDIA -TNAU (BMGF) Capacity Building on Cell Phone and Drone Data Collection and Processing
summary: The Capacity Building on Cell Phone and Drone Data Collection and Processing project aims to strengthen technical skills in digital agricultural data collection and analysis through the use of cell phone imagery and drone technologies. Implemented by the International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT) in collaboration with Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), and supported through funding from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, the project focuses on training participants in image-based data collection, drone data processing, and analytical techniques. Activities include virtual training sessions, practical assignments, mentoring, drone imagery analysis, and the development of visual data products to support agricultural research and decision-making. By enhancing participants’ capacity to collect, process, and interpret digital agricultural data, the project contributes to improved research methodologies, knowledge sharing, and the application of innovative technologies for agricultural development and sustainable food systems.

full_name: Greein Inc. (UNIDO) - Feasibility Study on a Data-Driven Circular Agribusiness Model
summary: The Data-Driven Circular Agribusiness Model for Sustainable Sunflower Production and Environmental Restoration project aims to assess the feasibility of innovative digital agriculture solutions that can improve sunflower productivity while supporting environmental restoration efforts in Ukraine. Implemented by the International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT) in collaboration with Greein Inc., FarmFleet, and Ivan Franko National University of Lviv, the initiative contributes to a United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) feasibility study. The project focuses on developing and validating AI-based cultivation algorithms, integrating agricultural IoT technologies, and generating data-driven insights to support more efficient and sustainable crop management. Through field monitoring, data collection, technical coordination, and analysis, the project seeks to demonstrate how digital technologies can enhance agricultural productivity while promoting circular economy principles and environmental sustainability in agricultural landscapes affected by ongoing climate and development challenges.

short_name: UNDP-M&E tools for insurance pilots
full_name: UNDP-M&E tools for insurance pilots
summary: Developing ME toolkits for UNDP insurance pilots in five countries: India, Bangladesh, Uganda, Tanzania and Ethiopia
description: The project involves developing an M&E toolkit and a global M&E framework for UNDP's insurance pilots — essentially building the measurement infrastructure to assess how inclusive insurance products are performing across markets. The work sits at the intersection of insurance systems design and results management, with the toolkit intended to standardize how outcomes are tracked and reported across UNDP-linked insurance interventions. It runs in parallel with a related UNDP insurance systems implementation workstream, where UNDP is building institutional infrastucture "Insurance desks" across multiple countries

short_name: Djibouti-MAFW-Programme to Strengthen Resilience to Food and Nutrition Insecurity ( BREFONS )
full_name: Djibouti-MAFW-Programme to Strengthen Resilience to Food and Nutrition Insecurity ( BREFONS )
summary: The Djibouti digital advisory pilot project supports climate-resilient agriculture by co-designing digital extension services with producers in Ali Sabieh and Tadjourah. Funded by the African Development Bank under the BREFONS initiative and implemented by Djibouti’s Ministry of Agriculture in partnership with the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, the pilot responds to drought, water scarcity, erratic rainfall, and food-import dependence. It is Djibouti’s first national experiment in digital agricultural extension, using tools such as interactive voice response, SMS tips, radio, WhatsApp, and short advisory videos. Co-design workshops with farmers, pastoralists, extension officers, women’s associations, meteorological agents, NGOs, and private-sector actors identified priority needs including seasonal forecasts, livestock health, soil moisture, and market prices. The project emphasizes local languages, voice-based communication, women’s and youth participation, open digital systems, and national institutional ownership. If successful, it could provide a scalable model for inclusive, climate-smart digital extension across the Horn of Africa.

short_name: PERU-STC-CGIAR-Innovaciones para prevención y el manejo del Fusarium raza 4 tropical (Foc R4T) en los cultivos de plátanos y bananos del Perú
full_name: PERU-STC-CGIAR-Innovaciones para prevención y el manejo del Fusarium raza 4 tropical (Foc R4T) en los cultivos de plátanos y bananos del Perú
summary:
The Alliance, in partnership with INIA, SENASA, and banana-producing communities in Peru, is implementing a project to develop and validate innovative strategies for the prevention and sustainable management of Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense Tropical Race 4 (Foc TR4). The initiative aims to prevent further spread of the pathogen in banana-based agricultural systems while generating scientific knowledge to strengthen national disease control strategies.
The project is structured around four objectives: (1) strengthening early detection through artificial intelligence and large-scale digital image analysis; (2) enriching, characterizing, and mass-producing native microorganisms with biocontrol potential against Foc TR4; (3) evaluating the suppressive effect of bioassays and cover crops against the pathogen; and (4) building capacity in affected and at-risk areas through training workshops and disease outbreak simulation exercises. Together, these components form an integrated approach combining digital innovation, biological control, and human capacity development to protect Peru's banana and plantain sector.

short_name: PERU-STC-CGIAR-Aplicacion de Tecnologia IoT para la Gestion de Enfermedades para la  Produccion Sostenible de Arroz en Peru bajo Condiciones Climaticas Cambiantes
full_name: PERU-STC-CGIAR-Aplicacion de Tecnologia IoT para la Gestion de Enfermedades para la  Produccion Sostenible de Arroz en Peru bajo Condiciones Climaticas Cambiantes
summary: The Application of IoT Technology for Disease Management in Sustainable Rice Production under Changing Climate Conditions project aims to improve the sustainability and resilience of rice production systems in Peru through the use of innovative digital technologies. Led by the International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT) in partnership with the National Agrarian University La Molina (UNALM), and supported through the STC-CGIAR competitive funding mechanism, the project focuses on applying Internet of Things (IoT) technologies to monitor, manage, and respond to crop disease risks under changing climatic conditions. The initiative seeks to enhance decision-making, improve disease surveillance, and strengthen the capacity of producers and stakeholders to adopt technology-based solutions. By integrating digital agriculture tools with research and extension activities, the project is expected to contribute to more sustainable rice production, improved productivity, and greater climate resilience in Peru’s rice-growing systems.

short_name: GERMANY-GIZ-AGB_SolNatura_Promoviendo Soluciones Basadas en la Naturaleza
full_name: GERMANY-GIZ-AGB_SolNatura_Promoviendo Soluciones Basadas en la Naturaleza
summary: This project supports the update of the Integrated Climate Change Management Plan for the Department of Huila, Colombia, through the generation of climate, vulnerability, emissions, and risk analyses that inform territorial decision-making. The initiative strengthens the evidence base required to align climate action with development planning and promotes collaboration among public institutions, private sector actors, academia, and civil society organizations. Through participatory processes and inclusive stakeholder engagement, it supports the integration of climate, biodiversity, gender, and social inclusion considerations into policy and planning frameworks. The project contributes to strengthened institutional capacities, improved climate governance, and more effective prioritization of adaptation and mitigation actions that support sustainable territorial development.

short_name: AgResearch (MPI)-Biological Nitrification Inhibition (BNI) for reducing N2O emissions from grazed livestock systems
full_name: AgResearch (MPI)-Biological Nitrification Inhibition (BNI) for reducing N2O emissions from grazed livestock systems
summary: This internship focused on supporting research on ammonia monooxygenase (amoA), a key enzyme involved in soil nitrification and nitrogen cycling, with implications for nitrogen losses and greenhouse gas emissions. The work aimed to strengthen understanding of ammonia-oxidising bacteria (AOB) and ammonia-oxidising archaea (AOA) populations in soil through molecular analysis. Activities included DNA quantification and standardisation, training in quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) techniques, quantification of amoA gene copy numbers in soil samples, data processing, and result analysis. The study generated baseline information on the abundance of nitrifying microorganisms, contributing to research on Biological Nitrification Inhibition (BNI) as a strategy to improve nitrogen-use efficiency, reduce nitrous oxide emissions, and enhance the environmental sustainability of agricultural systems.

short_name: UNDP-Strengthening the capacities of local financial institutions to integrate climate risks assessments into decision-making
full_name: UNDP-Strengthening the capacities of local financial institutions to integrate climate risks assessments into decision-making

full_name: Africa Rice (World Bank)-Appui à la transformation et à la résilience des systèmes alimentaires de Madagascar à travers la recherche pour le développement
summary: The Madagascar food systems resilience project is a research-for-development collaboration between AfricaRice and CIAT supporting transformation and resilience of food systems in Madagascar. The project is broader than breeding alone because it combines sustainable production, resilient seed systems, institutional capacity building, technology promotion and food system transformation. The strongest alignment is with Sustainable Farming and Breeding for Tomorrow, with an additional capacity-sharing component because the workplan includes training for FOFIFA, FIFAMANOR and SOC staff. short_name: Palladium International (Ireland-Irish Aid) Breeding to Business: Commercializing Improved  Common Bean Cultivars in Malawi (B2B)
full_name: Palladium International (Ireland-Irish Aid) Breeding to Business: Commercializing Improved  Common Bean Cultivars in Malawi (B2B)
summary: The Breeding to Business project is a public-private initiative to commercialize improved common bean cultivars in Malawi. It connects demand-led breeding with market adoption by evaluating sugar, navy and canning bean genotypes across Malawi's bean-growing agroecological zones together with private sector partners. The project will conduct on-farm participatory variety trials, produce nucleus seed, support variety release and licensing, strengthen seed scaling and develop structured grain market linkages. Its expected outputs include farmer-validated improved bean varieties, high-quality nucleus seed, formally released and scaled varieties, and a more structured bean market system. The project is strongly aligned with breeding modernization and scaling for impact, with additional relevance to food security and markets because it targets productivity, farmer income, nutrition security and regional trade opportunities.

short_name: IITA (USA-USAID) - Accelerated Innovation Delivery Initiative (AID-I) for Mozambique
full_name: IITA (USA-USAID) - Accelerated Innovation Delivery Initiative (AID-I) for Mozambique
summary: The AID-I Mozambique project supports accelerated delivery of bean innovations to improve food security, productivity, markets and nutrition in Mozambique. CIAT's work includes participatory variety selection for superior high-iron and climate-resilient bean varieties, on-farm demonstrations, promotion of released varieties, good bean production practices, early generation seed production, training of seed inspectors, integrated crop management technologies, bean business skills and structured market linkages. The workplan also includes nutrition-focused activities such as awareness on nutrient-dense beans, school gardens, cooking demonstrations and promotional materials. The project therefore combines breeding and variety evaluation, scaling and delivery, market linkages, seed systems, capacity building and nutrition outcomes.

short_name: SEDF-Assessing the social impacts of ABF investments in new business models in the Amazon.
full_name: SEDF-Assessing the social impacts of ABF investments in new business models in the Amazon.
summary: This project assesses the social impacts of investments made by the Amazon Biodiversity Fund (ABF) in new and emerging business models in the Brazilian Legal Amazon. ABF is a private, blended-finance impact fund co-designed by the Alliance, Impact Earth and development partners. The Soros Economic Development Fund (SEDF) is among its investors. The fund provides venture and early-stage growth finance to sustainable enterprises across pillars such as conservation and community livelihoods, smallholder value chains, sustainable agriculture, and innovation. The Alliance's role is to evaluate, understand and share the social additionality these investments generate for local and indigenous communities, drawing on monitoring approaches such as TerraBio. Major intended outcomes include rigorous evidence on how impact investments affect community wellbeing, income and social inclusion; improved monitoring methodologies for impact investing; and learning that strengthens the case for sustainable business models as an alternative to deforestation-driven economic activity in the Amazon.

short_name: BIUSA (Bezos Earth Fund)-Strengthening Forage Breeding Capacity to Deliver Low-Methane and Carbon-Sequestering Forages
full_name: BIUSA (Bezos Earth Fund)-Strengthening Forage Breeding Capacity to Deliver Low-Methane and Carbon-Sequestering Forages
summary: This project aims to strengthen forage breeding capacity to develop and promote innovative forage varieties that reduce methane emissions and enhance carbon sequestration. By advancing research and breeding efforts, the initiative supports the transition toward more sustainable and climate-resilient livestock systems, contributing to greenhouse gas mitigation, improved environmental performance, and long-term agricultural sustainability.

short_name: FSD-Restauracion integral con enfoque de cadena de valor
full_name: FSD-Restauracion integral con enfoque de cadena de valor
summary: Fomentar el uso de especies nativas de calidad en los procesos de restauración del Bosque Seco Tropical (BST) a través de la creación de una red comunitaria de recolectores y el establecimiento de huertos semilleros que permitan la realización de plantaciones forestales que involucren un enfoque comunitario y de cadena de valor.

short_name: Rockefeller Foundation-Advancing translation and impact of the Periodic Table of Food Initiative (PTFI) (IA Lead of A1684)
full_name: Rockefeller Foundation-Advancing translation and impact of the Periodic Table of Food Initiative (PTFI) (IA Lead of A1684)
summary:
The Periodic Table of Food Initiative (PTFI) is a global effort to advance the characterization of food biodiversity and biomolecular composition to support healthier, more sustainable, and resilient food systems. The project aims to expand the scientific and practical value of PTFI data by developing new metrics, visualizations, and metadata that link food composition with nutrition, health, climate, and environmental outcomes. Through standardized tools, data resources, and training, the initiative enables researchers, policymakers, and practitioners to generate evidence-based solutions to challenges such as malnutrition, biodiversity loss, and climate change.
Expected outcomes include increased global use of PTFI data and tools, improved understanding of the links between food composition and health, stronger international research collaboration, enhanced data governance and equity, and greater capacity to inform policies and practices that promote sustainable food systems and human well-being.
