short_name: SAHEL CONSULTING-Building sustainable climate monitoring and addressing early warning system bottlenecks for resilient agricultural systems in Nigeria
full_name: SAHEL CONSULTING-Building sustainable climate monitoring and addressing early warning system bottlenecks for resilient agricultural systems in Nigeria
summary: The Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation (the “Funding Partner”) has engaged Sahel to implement the EWS Project. The Project will be implemented in conjunction with the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet), the International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT), International Research Institute for Climate and Society (IRI), and other climate stakeholders. CIAT and IRI are two of the Project’s subcontracting organizations. The Project will have a steering committee which will be chaired by the Director General of NiMet.

short_name: Rockefeller Foundation-Nourishing Minds and Soils: Regenerative Approaches to School Nutrition
full_name: Rockefeller Foundation-Nourishing Minds and Soils: Regenerative Approaches to School Nutrition
summary: The project aims to strengthen school feeding systems by integrating regenerative agriculture, nutrition, and education in rural communities in Kenya. Led by the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, the project focuses on generating scientific evidence on how regenerative farming practices affect the productivity and nutritional quality of biofortified high-iron Nyota beans under smallholder conditions. Building on previous work in Embu County, the initiative combines field research, farmer engagement, and school-based learning to promote climate-resilient and sustainable food systems. The project will develop practical tools for farmers, establish school demonstration plots, and create educational materials linking agriculture, nutrition, and environmental sustainability. Through these efforts, the project seeks to improve nutrition outcomes, strengthen farmer livelihoods, enhance resilience to climate change, and provide scalable models for integrating regenerative agriculture into school meal programs.

short_name: John Templeton Foundation-Scoping grant assessing strategies for agricultural transformation of orphan crops in Latin America
full_name: John Templeton Foundation-Scoping grant assessing strategies for agricultural transformation of orphan crops in Latin America
summary: This grant will propose a portfolio of regional projects that reflect a whole-of-value-chain approach for 4 key orphan crops (Chia, Passiflora, Quinoa, Yacon), complemented by 6-8 targeted initiatives that will be crop and country specific. The key crops were identified during our landscaping analysis and have been selected based on their economic and nutritional potential. The projects will aim to leverage and add value to ongoing initiatives and will have, at core, an emphasis on mitigating the impacts of climate change and on sustainability i.e. the development of human capacity while preserving cultural heritage and biodiversity. A key output of this grant will be an elaborated Request for Proposals (RFP) that may result in an orphan crop investment portfolio of about $4M over 3 years that will boost economic development and climate resilience in Latin America.

short_name: IITA (GATES FOUDATION) Development of Broad-Spectrum Rice Blast Resistance through Quantum-Enhanced Gene Stacking and Polymerization
full_name: IITA (GATES FOUDATION) Development of Broad-Spectrum Rice Blast Resistance through Quantum-Enhanced Gene Stacking and Polymerization
summary: The CGIAR Genetic Innovations Public-Private Partnership Platform project focuses on developing broad-spectrum rice blast resistance through quantum-enhanced gene stacking and polymerization. Implemented by CIAT as a subgrantee of IITA with Gates Foundation support, the project combines genomics, phenomics, transcriptomics, artificial intelligence, and haplotype analysis to identify and stack resistance genes in rice. Key activities include curating SNP and blast phenotypic data for 3,000 rice accessions, conducting GWAS and AI-based analyses, developing RNA sequencing protocols, completing transcriptomic analysis, and identifying resistance gene stacks.

short_name: University of California (BMGF)-GEMINI : GxExM Innovation in Intelligence for climate adaptations
full_name: University of California (BMGF)-GEMINI : GxExM Innovation in Intelligence for climate adaptations
summary: The GEMINI project focuses on developing next-generation breeding analytics that link crop product concepts to varietal field performance under climate stress. CIAT’s role, through the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, is to support common bean research in East Africa by conducting field evaluations in Tanzania and Uganda. The work includes testing interspecific bean lines derived from common bean, tepary bean, and runner bean across contrasting environmental conditions, with attention to heat, drought, productivity, nutritional quality, and cooking time. CIAT will also support testing of sensing devices, field management, sample collection for nutritional phenotyping, data analysis, and participation in project coordination. The project integrates social science and gender-responsive activities, including the development of product profiles and characterization of end-user demographics and preferences.

short_name: WRI (Denmark-MoFA) - Empowering Ethiopian Smallholder Farmers through Climate-Smart Agriculture
full_name: WRI (Denmark-MoFA) - Empowering Ethiopian Smallholder Farmers through Climate-Smart Agriculture
summary: The project shall demonstrate the effectiveness of leveraging digital tools and an agent network to scale the adoption of geo-location-specific fertilizer recommendations, integrated with financial services, among smallholder farmers, thereby enhancing agricultural productivity and income during the funding period (the “Project”), as set forth in more detail in Attachment 1B. Subrecipient will use best efforts towards the achievement of the goals of the Project, all of which shall be consistent with WRI’s charitable mission of moving human society to live in ways that protect Earth’s environment and its capacity to provide for the needs and aspirations of current and future generations.

short_name: GGGI (BMGF)-Strengthening Financial Institutions Capacity for Climate-Smart Lending in West Africa
full_name: GGGI (BMGF)-Strengthening Financial Institutions Capacity for Climate-Smart Lending in West Africa
summary: Under the GGGI–EBID Agricultural Adaptation Facility (AAF), financial institutions (FIs) in West Africa are being supported to strengthen their capacity to assess climate risks, design climate-smart financial products, and scale lending for climate adaptation across agriculture and agri-SME value chains.
description: Deliver climate analytics portfolio diagnostic of financial instituions and support them to structure and design climate financing bundles that enhance farmer and agribusiness resilience to climate risks

short_name: WRI (Denmark-MOFA) - Building Resilience Through Warehouse Receipt System in Kenya
full_name: WRI (Denmark-MOFA) - Building Resilience Through Warehouse Receipt System in Kenya
summary: The project Building Resilience of Farmers Through Warehouse Receipt System in Kenya aims to improve food security, farmer incomes, and climate resilience by reducing post-harvest losses through a Warehouse Receipt System. Running from April 2025 to March 2027 in Kenya, the project is funded by P4G and implemented through a partnership between agriBORA and the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT. Its WRS model, called agriGHALA, enables farmers in climate-vulnerable areas to store produce in climate-controlled warehouses and sell when market prices are more favorable. The project will operationalize storage facilities in Kisumu and Eldoret, promote farmer awareness and trust, and connect smallholders to commodity-backed financing. It also provides access to quality inputs, climate-smart agriculture training, and market linkages. By improving storage, finance, and market access, the project seeks to strengthen income stability, reduce food losses, and lower farming’s carbon footprint.

short_name: WTW-De-Risking Coffee From Climate Disasters: Upscaling Coffee Climate Protection Insurance For Vietnamese Smallholder Coffee Producers
full_name: WTW-De-Risking Coffee From Climate Disasters: Upscaling Coffee Climate Protection Insurance For Vietnamese Smallholder Coffee Producers
summary: The WTW-led "De-Risking Coffee from Climate Disasters" project upscales the Coffee Climate Protection Insurance - a parametric, index-based weather insurance scheme covering drought and excess rainfall - from its initial pilot in Dak Lak and Lam Dong to all five Central Highlands provinces (now consolidated into three: Dak Lak, Gia Lai, and Lam Dong), targeting smallholder Robusta coffee producers with a goal of 5,000 insurance policies. Key outcomes include improved climate risk management through climate-smart agriculture (CSA) integration, and a sustainable co-subsidized insurance premium model shared across farmers, traders, and roasters. Partners include WTW and Global Parametrics (product development  and reinsurance), the University of Southern Queensland (risk modelling, co-subsidy models, and high level engagement), the Alliance (Willingness to Pay study, CSA, M&E, and farmer communications), and Atlantic Commodities Vietnam/ECOM (distribution via its farmer network), with Bao Minh Insurance providing local fronting and a digital policy registration platform.
description: The WTW-led "De-Risking Coffee from Climate Disasters" project, funded by the InsuResilience Solutions Fund (January 2025–January 2027), upscales the Coffee Climate Protection Insurance (CCPI) — a parametric, index-based weather insurance scheme covering drought and excess rainfall — from its initial pilot in Dak Lak and Lam Dong to all five Central Highlands provinces (now consolidated into three: Dak Lak, Gia Lai, and Lam Dong), targeting smallholder Robusta coffee producers with a goal of 5,000 insurance policies. short_name: ILRI (GERMANY-GIZ) - Catalyzing transformation towards sustainable livestock systems (LiveSys)
full_name: ILRI (GERMANY-GIZ) - Catalyzing transformation towards sustainable livestock systems (LiveSys)
summary: The Catalyzing Transformation Towards Sustainable Livestock Systems (LiveSys) project aims to mobilize finance, partnerships, and knowledge to support sustainable livestock development in Africa and Asia. Implemented by CIAT in collaboration with ILRI, the project focuses on identifying agricultural finance and climate investment opportunities that can help transform livestock systems while improving resilience, sustainability, and livelihoods. CIAT will assess public and private finance mechanisms, identify barriers and opportunities, and develop project proposals that can attract funding for livestock-related climate and development investments. The project will also provide technical assistance to develop at least two projects through the landscape analysis and support knowledge exchange through workshops, study tours, and training materials.

short_name: USA-USAID-Emerging topics in MRV, finance, data, and digital tools for NDC investment and implementation
full_name: USA-USAID-Emerging topics in MRV, finance, data, and digital tools for NDC investment and implementation
summary: Innovation for LED food systems, with a focus on (1) carbon markets and (2) mutidimensional tipping point thresholds for food systems.
description: Scientific paper on the state of the voluntary carbon market for agrifood, a paper with partners on tipping point analysis with specially explicit maps, and grant writing and pre-project team management for Gates Foundation' Big Bet on carbon credits for adaptation.

short_name: Clifford Chance-Sustainable School Feeding Innovations in Kigali
full_name: Clifford Chance-Sustainable School Feeding Innovations in Kigali
summary: The project is designed to strengthen local food security through combined agricultural, nutrition, monitoring, and digital support activities. Its budget structure indicates work around expert technical assistance, planning and review meetings, training for schools on nutrition and farming practices, and provision of equipment and materials, including micro-irrigation support. The project also includes digital deployment, local travel, supplies, computers, and multistakeholder engagement, suggesting an integrated approach that connects technical delivery with coordination and field implementation. Reporting requirements emphasize progress, impact achieved, budget execution, and accountability to the donor and Charities Aid Foundation. Overall, the project appears focused on improving food security outcomes by combining capacity building, practical farming support, nutrition education, monitoring, and partnerships in Kigali for vulnerable communities and school stakeholders

short_name: Japan-UTokyo (BRAIN) Evaluation of the effects of rice candidate genes on drought resistance in the field environment
full_name: Japan-UTokyo (BRAIN) Evaluation of the effects of rice candidate genes on drought resistance in the field environment
summary: The Evaluation of Rice Candidate Genes for Drought Resistance in Field Conditions project aims to validate the role of promising rice genes associated with drought tolerance under real-world field environments. Conducted by the International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT) in collaboration with the University of Tokyo and the Bio-oriented Technology Research Advancement Institution (BRAIN) of Japan, the project focuses on assessing candidate genes previously identified in japonica rice varieties and evaluating their performance in indica rice backgrounds. Using genome-edited rice lines and controlled drought stress experiments under field conditions, the research seeks to generate scientific evidence on the genetic mechanisms that contribute to drought resilience. The project is expected to advance knowledge for the development of climate-resilient rice varieties, supporting future breeding efforts and contributing to sustainable agricultural systems that can better adapt to increasing water scarcity and climate variability.

short_name: ROCKFOUND Valle Regenerative Hub: AI-Powered Monitoring and Collective Action
full_name: ROCKFOUND Valle Regenerative Hub: AI-Powered Monitoring and Collective Action
summary: The Regenerative Agriculture Knowledge-Sharing Hub project aims to strengthen the adoption and impact of regenerative agriculture practices in Colombia by developing a collaborative platform that supports knowledge generation, monitoring, and learning. Led by the International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT) with support from The Rockefeller Foundation, the project focuses on building a coalition of stakeholders, establishing a regenerative agriculture knowledge hub, and generating scientific evidence on soil health, biodiversity, and microbiome indicators. The initiative also seeks to strengthen connections between regenerative agriculture and school feeding programs, promoting more sustainable and nutritious food systems. Through data collection, capacity building, open-access knowledge products, and stakeholder engagement, the project is expected to improve the measurement and understanding of regenerative agriculture outcomes while supporting broader adoption of sustainable farming practices that benefit producers, communities, and the environment in Colombia.

short_name: GCA (GAC)-Program for Advancing gender responsive and sustainable digital climate advisory services.
full_name: GCA (GAC)-Program for Advancing gender responsive and sustainable digital climate advisory services.
summary: This project aims to advance gender-responsive and sustainable Digital Climate Advisory Services (DCAS) in Africa through targeted case studies in Malawi, Ethiopia, and Rwanda. Led by CIAT, the project combines climate science, gender analysis, digital agriculture, business model assessment, and stakeholder engagement to identify practical ways to scale DCAS for women farmers and vulnerable groups. It will review best practices, assess gender integration in the Adaptation Atlas, and analyze three DCAS models: a public-sector model in Malawi, a public-private platform in Ethiopia, and a private-sector approach in Rwanda. The project will produce implementation guidelines, business case guidance, country case study reports, videos, and dissemination materials. It will also convene financial institutions, private sector actors, policymakers, and implementers to explore financing, sustainability, and policy needs. Overall, the project seeks to strengthen stakeholder capacity and support inclusive, evidence-based scaling of climate advisory services across Africa.

short_name: IITA (BI-UK FCDO) - A Climate-Smart Agronomy Vision for Adapted Crops and Soils (AgVACS). Supporting smallholder farmer decision making through participatory experimental-modelling networks  in West Africa
full_name: IITA (BI-UK FCDO) - A Climate-Smart Agronomy Vision for Adapted Crops and Soils (AgVACS). Supporting smallholder farmer decision making through participatory experimental-modelling networks  in West Africa
summary: This project integrates VACS crops into climate-smart agronomy to improve productivity, resilience and sustainability of smallholder farming systems in Ghana and Nigeria.

short_name: WUR (Nestle) - Ground Zero
full_name: WUR (Nestle) - Ground Zero
summary: The Ground Zero project seeks to: Benchmark carbon footprints, soil health and biodiversity in cocoa and coffee production and primary processing at source of origin; Provide a series of robust, easily measurable and verifiable indicators and tools that can be deployed for monitoring in cocoa and coffee supply chains; and Explore opportunities to achieve positive impacts on carbon footprints, soil health and biodiversity in cocoa and coffee production and primary processing. The project conducts baseline measurements and on-farm field experiments with different fertilisation strategies and organic amendments for greenhouse gas emissions and soil health, and biodiversity assessments comparing different production system types in Mexico, Colombia and Zambia for coffee, and Ecuador and Ivory Coast for cocoa. The project is led by Wageningen University and Research in collaboration with the Nestlé Institute of Agricultural Sciences (NIAS), Olam Food Ingredients, the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT and ETH Zurich.

short_name: IWMI-(USA-USAID)-Water and Soil Accelerator ‘Sustainable soil and water management from farm to landscape.’
full_name: IWMI-(USA-USAID)-Water and Soil Accelerator ‘Sustainable soil and water management from farm to landscape.’
summary: The Water and Soil Accelerator is a USAID-funded cooperative agreement led/managed by the International Water Management Institute (IWMI), running 2024–2027. Its purpose is to scale sustainable water and soil management practices from farm to landscape level in rainfed systems, with a focus on poor and women smallholder farmers in Feed the Future Zones of Influence in Zambia and Malawi. Focusing on Zambia the Alliance through our main project implementation partners Mediae, Solidaridad and One Acre Fund is contributing to the delivery of Climate Information Services, PICSA, Climate Smart Agriculture training and Rangeland Management systems to beneficiary farmers.

short_name: IRLANDA-DFAT-Expanding the Climate Security Observatory (CSO) as a decision support tool to policymakers in Honduras (IA Lead of A1761)
full_name: IRLANDA-DFAT-Expanding the Climate Security Observatory (CSO) as a decision support tool to policymakers in Honduras (IA Lead of A1761)
summary: The project aims to influence national and local policy processes in Honduras to reduce climate-driven insecurity by expanding the CGIAR Climate Security Observatory to the country. It will generate and disseminate actionable evidence on how, where and for whom climate risks intersect with fragility, conflict, displacement and migration. Using mixed qualitative and quantitative methods, including climate security pathway analysis, participatory approaches, network analysis, mediation modelling and hotspot mapping, the project will identify key risk pathways and vulnerable areas. It will also support partners to assess current policies, programmes and financing through tools such as policy coherence analysis, the Climate Security Sensitivity Tool and governance diagnostics. Based on this evidence, the project will co-develop conflict-sensitive strategies, provide technical assistance and capacity building, and support the integration of climate security considerations into adaptation interventions, policy documents and strategic plans at regional, national and local levels.

short_name: HHU (BMGF) - Transformative Strategy for Controlling Rice Disease in Developing Countries, Phase III
full_name: HHU (BMGF) - Transformative Strategy for Controlling Rice Disease in Developing Countries, Phase III
summary: The project aims to develop, validate, and transfer genome-edited rice varieties with durable resistance to bacterial blight and rice blast, two major diseases that significantly reduce rice productivity in Africa and Asia. Led by Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf in collaboration with international partners including the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, KALRO, IRD, and several research institutions, the project focuses on applying advanced genome editing technologies to create disease-resistant elite rice lines and support their evaluation under field conditions. The project also strengthens scientific capacity through technology transfer, training, pathogen surveillance, and regulatory preparedness in target countries. By enabling the development and dissemination of improved rice germplasm, the initiative seeks to enhance food security, reduce crop losses, and provide smallholder farmers with resilient rice varieties adapted to current and emerging disease threats.

short_name: 3iE-Policy Sprint Labs as a pathway to enhance evidence-driven policies on food-system informal micro and small enterprises in Kenya and Ethiopia
full_name: 3iE-Policy Sprint Labs as a pathway to enhance evidence-driven policies on food-system informal micro and small enterprises in Kenya and Ethiopia
summary: This FCDO-funded project (January 2026–December 2027) examines whether Evidence-to-Policy Sprints (EPS) can improve evidence-informed policymaking on informal micro and small enterprises (IMSEs) in food systems in Kenya and Ethiopia. Despite the economic and social importance of IMSEs, policy debates surrounding these actors are often shaped by competing narratives, political considerations, and limited use of empirical evidence. The project combines Knowledge Translation and Exchange (KTE) interventions with structured policy dialogues to improve policymakers’ awareness, access to, and use of research evidence. Guided by the Theory of Planned Behaviour, the evaluation uses a small-N baseline–endline design to assess changes in policymakers’ attitudes, subjective norms, perceived behavioural control, and intentions to use evidence. The study also explores the contextual, institutional, political, and cognitive factors that influence evidence uptake, contributing new knowledge on both the effectiveness of policy sprints and the determinants of evidence-informed policymaking in low- and middle-income country contexts.

short_name: Democratic Republic of Congo -Ministere de L'Agriculture (AfDB) Support Project for the Development of Agricultural Value Chains in Six Provinces (PADCA- 6P)
full_name: Democratic Republic of Congo -Ministere de L'Agriculture (AfDB) Support Project for the Development of Agricultural Value Chains in Six Provinces (PADCA- 6P)
summary: The project supports the production and dissemination of biofortified beans with high nutritional value in the Haut-Lomami Province of the Democratic Republic of Congo, within the PADCA-6P intervention area. Implemented by CIAT in collaboration with PADCA-6P, the initiative aims to improve food and nutrition security while increasing the income of farming households. Its work focuses on producing certified pre-basic and basic bean seed, introducing and disseminating biofortified varieties in farming communities, and strengthening the capacities of value-chain actors. The project promotes improved agricultural practices, post-harvest management, processing, storage, and commercialization of biofortified beans. It also emphasizes the participation of women, youth, and vulnerable groups, recognizing their role in resilient agricultural systems. Through field days, training, demonstrations, and technical support, the project seeks to expand access to nutritious bean varieties, improve seed availability, build local expertise, and contribute to climate adaptation and sustainable rural development in the target territory and communities.

short_name: BIUSA (SALL FAMILY) - Unrestricted Future Seeds Programming
full_name: BIUSA (SALL FAMILY) - Unrestricted Future Seeds Programming
summary: This unrestricted BIUSA/Sall Family Foundation grant supports Future Seeds programming, including the conservation, study and deployment of vital crops through CIAT's state-of-the-art genebank. The agreement describes Future Seeds as a response to the need for expanded capacity for CIAT's existing genebank, which holds more than 67,000 samples from 141 countries. The strongest alignment is with Genebank because the project directly supports genetic resources conservation, study and deployment. It also has a secondary relationship with Breeding for Tomorrow where conserved and characterized germplasm supports crop improvement pipelines, and with Capacity Sharing where outreach, partnerships or research strategy activities strengthen use of genetic resources.

short_name: PABRA Al Sumait Prize Award (Kuwait)
full_name: PABRA Al Sumait Prize Award (Kuwait)
summary: The PABRA Al-Sumait Prize Award recognizes the Pan Africa Bean Research Alliance for establishing, coordinating and serving a dynamic network of scientists, practitioners and partners across Africa. The award highlights PABRA's contribution to developing improved bean varieties and sustainable markets that enhance food security, income and nutrition for smallholder farmers and urban dwellers. Based on the available certificate, the project is best understood as institutional recognition and support for a regional bean research and development network, rather than a narrowly defined research trial. The strongest alignment is with Capacity Sharing because the award is linked to network coordination, scientific collaboration, partner engagement and knowledge exchange.

short_name: IFAD-Alianza de Aprendizaje para fortalecer las capacidades para la evaluación participativa y mejora en cadenas de valor y alianzas comerciales inclusivas a lo interno del proyecto FIDA PROINORTE en Honduras
full_name: IFAD-Alianza de Aprendizaje para fortalecer las capacidades para la evaluación participativa y mejora en cadenas de valor y alianzas comerciales inclusivas a lo interno del proyecto FIDA PROINORTE en Honduras
summary:
The PROINORTE project, funded by IFAD and implemented by the Honduran Ministry of Agriculture, seeks to improve incomes, nutrition, and resilience among smallholder farmers in northeastern Honduras. The US$46.5 million initiative reaches approximately 15,000 rural households across 22 municipalities.

Through a US$500,000 grant, the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT supports PROINORTE in strengthening its nutrition-sensitive approach and institutional capacities. The grant promotes participatory, food systems–based methodologies aligned with Honduras’ Food Systems Transformation Roadmap through technical assistance, capacity building, and implementation support.

The Alliance’s work focuses on three areas: (1) developing municipal food systems profiles to inform local planning and investment priorities; (2) integrating nutrition considerations into value chain analysis and development; and (3) embedding nutrition, gender, and inclusion into farmer business plans and investment processes. Together, these efforts strengthen the capacity to design and implement more nutrition-sensitive and inclusive rural development investments.
description:
The PROINORTE project (Proyecto de Inclusión Económica y Social de Pequeños Productores Rurales en la Región Noreste de Honduras), funded by the International Fund for Agricultural Development and implemented by the Honduran Ministry of Agriculture, aims to improve incomes, nutrition, and resilience among smallholder farmers by strengthening productive capacities and facilitating market inclusion. The US$46.5 million program reaches approximately 15,000 rural households across 22 municipalities in northeastern Honduras.

Within PROINORTE, the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT implements a US$500,000 grant focused on strengthening the project’s nutrition-sensitive design and implementation. The grant builds capacities within government and partners to apply participatory, food systems–based approaches aligned with Honduras’ Food Systems Transformation Roadmap. It combines technical assistance, on-the-ground implementation support, and learning to enable scaling within the Ministry and across other IFAD investments.

The Alliance’s support focuses on three areas:

1.Municipal food systems profiling: Adapting and applying a food systems lens at the municipal level to diagnose constraints and prioritize interventions. This included piloting in two municipalities and scaling to 20 more, informing local planning and project targeting. 
2.Nutrition-sensitive value chains: Integrating nutrition objectives into value chain analysis and development by adapting IFAD methodologies and building capacity among Ministry staff and service providers to identify interventions that improve both competitiveness and diets. 
3.Inclusive business models: Embedding nutrition, gender, and inclusion into farmer business plans through improved tools, review processes, and training, alongside the development of a digital system to manage and monitor over 160 business plans. 

Together, these efforts strengthen the institutional capacity to design and deliver agriculture investments that contribute not only to incomes, but also to improved diets and more inclusive, resilient food systems.

short_name: WFP-LTA Global Research Services – HDP nexus
full_name: WFP-LTA Global Research Services – HDP nexus
summary: In Cabo Delgado, Mozambique, CGIAR and WFP co-developed a conflict-sensitive, nature-based solution approach to support livelihood recovery interventions in Palma and Mocímboa da Praia. Using integrated ecosystem assessment across 10 communities, supported by spatial and scenario modelling, combined with participatory conflict-sensitive analysis in the two districts, the initiative identified Nature-based Solutions that restore livelihoods without exacerbating further tensions. The results directly inform WFP programmes reaching ~7,000 households, demonstrating how environmental restoration can advance social stability, resilience, and humanitarian recovery in climate and conflict-affected contexts.
description: Capacity building of the last mile on Digital Climate Advisory Services & climate resilient seeds.

short_name: IDRC (AUSTRALIA-ACIAR)-Scaling the impacts of pre-cooked bean innovations in Kenya and Uganda (Beannovate Project)
full_name: IDRC (AUSTRALIA-ACIAR)-Scaling the impacts of pre-cooked bean innovations in Kenya and Uganda (Beannovate Project)
summary: The Beannovate Project aims to scale the impact of improved bean varieties and pre-cooked bean products in Kenya and Uganda. The project seeks to strengthen the capacity and understanding of farmers, value chain actors, and consumers, with emphasis on men, women, and youth. Its objectives are to increase productivity and income gains from improved bean varieties; expand consumption of pre-cooked bean-based products by addressing adoption barriers and improving supply-chain efficiency; enhance women’s and youth participation, leadership, and decision-making across bean value chains; and strengthen public-private partnerships to stimulate investment and job creation

short_name: GATES AG ONE Long Term Research Agreement Bill & Melinda Gates Agricultural Innovations
full_name: GATES AG ONE Long Term Research Agreement Bill & Melinda Gates Agricultural Innovations
summary: This long-term research agreement with Gates Ag One covers research and development activities to translate early-stage innovations into products for commercially relevant crops for smallholder farmers and global access. The agreement includes seed and plant receipt, quality testing, assay optimization, greenhouse or field increases, regulated and conventional field trials, genotyping studies and analysis, plant transformation, storage and shipment of materials, and studies related to cooking quality. The strongest alignment is with Breeding for Tomorrow because the work supports crop improvement, transformation, genotyping, trials and product-oriented breeding research. It also aligns with Scaling for Impact through translation of innovations into products and global access for smallholder farmers. Better Diets and Nutrition may be relevant where work plans include cooking quality or end-use quality studies.

short_name: IU-Ibaraki University-M4NCO-Microbe mediated methane mitigation, nitrogen cycle optimization
full_name: IU-Ibaraki University-M4NCO-Microbe mediated methane mitigation, nitrogen cycle optimization
summary: The Methane-Oxidizing Microbe-Mediated Methane Mitigation and Nitrogen Cycle Optimization project aims to develop innovative microbial solutions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and improve nitrogen-use efficiency in rice production systems. Led by Ibaraki University in collaboration with the International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT) and supported by the Gates Foundation, the project focuses on identifying and evaluating beneficial microorganisms that can mitigate methane emissions while enhancing crop productivity and sustainability. Through laboratory, greenhouse, and field-based research, the project will generate scientific knowledge, methodologies, and microbial technologies for climate-smart rice cultivation. The expected outcomes include reduced environmental impacts from rice farming, improved nutrient management practices, and scalable solutions that can contribute to sustainable agricultural development and climate change mitigation in rice-growing regions across Asia and beyond.

short_name: IITA (USA-USAID) - Accelerated Innovation Delivery Initiative – AID-I: Great Lakes Highlands
full_name: IITA (USA-USAID) - Accelerated Innovation Delivery Initiative – AID-I: Great Lakes Highlands
summary: The work of this project focuses overall on scaling access to high-iron, biofortified bean seed and strengthening seed systems in Rwanda, Burundi, and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Activities include identifying seed companies, agro-dealers, decentralized seed producers, demand for early generation seed, developing seed distribution roadmaps, training producers, and promoting climate-smart bean varieties through radio talks, field days, demonstrations, and open forums.

short_name: SPAIN-AECID-Restauración agroecológica y tecnológica de  cafetales en paisajes productivos caracterizados por la migración y feminización (IA Lead of A1789)
full_name: SPAIN-AECID-Restauración agroecológica y tecnológica de  cafetales en paisajes productivos caracterizados por la migración y feminización (IA Lead of A1789)
summary: The project “Restauracion agroecologicaRestauración agroecológica de cafetales inclusiva y apoyada en innovación tecnológica en contextos de migración y feminización, Matagalpa, Nicaragua” aims to strengthen a more inclusive, sustainable, and resilient coffee sector in Nicaragua. Implemented by CIAT between 2026 and 2028 with funding from AECID (€500,000), the initiative focuses on smallholder coffee producers in the municipalities of San Ramón and La Dalia, Matagalpa, with special attention to women and youth affected by migration and the increasing feminization of agricultural labor.
description: The project seeks to improve technical, organizational, and productive capacities through training, technical assistance, and the promotion of agroecological practices that enhance productivity, climate resilience, and environmental sustainability. In collaboration with IPSA and five local coffee cooperatives, the project will support the rehabilitation and diversification of approximately 300 coffee farms covering at least 200 hectares, including the use of certified planting material and climate-smart management practices.

short_name: FAO-Servicios de consultoría para un Analisis de vulnerabilidad para elaborar planes de Adaptación Basada en Ecosistemas (ABE)
full_name: FAO-Servicios de consultoría para un Analisis de vulnerabilidad para elaborar planes de Adaptación Basada en Ecosistemas (ABE)
summary: This project develops climate vulnerability assessments, modeling analyses, and adaptation planning tools to support ecosystem-based adaptation strategies across multiple countries in Central America and the Dominican Republic. Through the generation of climate, environmental, and socioeconomic evidence, it supports the identification of climate risks, adaptation priorities, and resilient livelihood options within selected watersheds. The initiative strengthens the capacity of national and local stakeholders to incorporate climate information into planning and decision-making processes while supporting the development of context-specific adaptation pathways. By providing robust analytical foundations and decision-support tools, the project contributes to improved resilience planning, informed investments, and the integration of adaptation considerations into ecosystem management and development strategies.
description: Developing knowledge and analytics on climate risks in support of Digital Climate Advisory Services (DCAS) and scaling up climate resilient seeds

short_name: STARBUCKS - Developing contextualized recommendations for soil health enhancing practices and carbon footprint reductions in coffee cultivation
full_name: STARBUCKS - Developing contextualized recommendations for soil health enhancing practices and carbon footprint reductions in coffee cultivation
summary: This project supports Starbucks and its coffee supply chain partners in transitioning to regenerative agriculture by developing contextualized soil health and fertilizer management recommendations across nine coffee-producing countries: Colombia, Peru, Honduras, Guatemala, El Salvador, Costa Rica, Uganda, Mexico, and Indonesia (Sumatra). Alliance applies Digital Soil Mapping (DSM) approaches — integrating field soil measurements with spatial data and previously developed soil inference systems — to generate site-specific, data-driven guidance for coffee growers.Key aimed impacts include improved fertilizer use efficiency, enhanced soil health, and reduced carbon footprint of coffee production, directly contributing to Starbucks' commitment to Carbon Neutral Green Coffee by 2030. Deliverables include high-resolution digital soil maps in GIS format and tailored soil health and fertilizer recommendations for each country, spanning diverse agroecological contexts across Latin America, East Africa, and Southeast Asia.

short_name: GCA (Germany-GIZ)-Technical Services to Support Climate Adaptation in the Food Security Sector of Africa & South Asia (Framework Agreement)
full_name: GCA (Germany-GIZ)-Technical Services to Support Climate Adaptation in the Food Security Sector of Africa & South Asia (Framework Agreement)

short_name: Australia-ACIAR-Supporting the regional Asia Cassava Breeding and Disease Surveillance Network
full_name: Australia-ACIAR-Supporting the regional Asia Cassava Breeding and Disease Surveillance Network
summary: This project supports the development and delivery of late-stage cassava breeding products in Southeast Asia while strengthening the development and operationalization of the Asian Cassava Breeding Network. Key activities include capacity development, technical support, germplasm exchange, breeding network coordination, and strategic guidance, with a particular focus on sharing late-stage breeding materials and accelerating variety development across partner programs.

short_name: Australia-ACIAR-Demand Led Capacity Building Framework for the Bean Corridor Approach Project
full_name: Australia-ACIAR-Demand Led Capacity Building Framework for the Bean Corridor Approach Project
summary: The ACIAR Demand Led Capacity Building Framework for the Bean Corridor Approach supports the PABRA Academy and strengthens the capacity of national partners working in bean value chains. The partnership focuses on young scientists, students and research teams by supporting tuition, research costs, working groups, interdisciplinary research, collaborative study design, proposal development and harmonization of research across partner countries. Its scientific contribution is connected to demand-led breeding, crop management, inclusive agri-enterprise development and stakeholder engagement. The project is primarily a capacity-sharing and partnership-strengthening initiative, with a secondary link to breeding modernization because the capacity development is focused on bean crop improvement for value chain development. It should contribute to 2026 reporting through capacity, research collaboration and learning outputs.

short_name: BIUSA (SALL FAMILY) - Unrestricted Future Seeds Program and PABRA
full_name: BIUSA (SALL FAMILY) - Unrestricted Future Seeds Program and PABRA
summary: This unrestricted BIUSA/Sall Family Foundation grant supports two main areas of Alliance work: core support for the Future Seeds Program and support to the Pan Africa Bean Research Alliance (PABRA) for women's enterprises. The agreement allocates activities running from March 2024 to March 2026 and final narrative and financial reports due in May 2026. The strongest alignment is with Genebank through Future Seeds core support. A secondary alignment is with Gender Equality and Inclusion because the PABRA component specifically supports women's enterprises. A smaller strategic link to Scaling for Impact may apply through enterprise support and delivery pathways.

short_name: IRRI-SGP GENOME EDITING-Accelerating Crop Improvement through Genome Editing
full_name: IRRI-SGP GENOME EDITING-Accelerating Crop Improvement through Genome Editing
summary: The Accelerating Crop Improvement through Genome Editing project aims to advance the development and application of genome editing technologies to accelerate crop improvement and support sustainable agricultural innovation. Implemented by the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT in collaboration with the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) and CGIAR partners, the project focuses on developing genome editing protocols, stewardship frameworks, product concepts, and regulatory pathways for foreign DNA-free genome-edited crops. The initiative also strengthens capacity development, promotes collaboration with national agricultural research systems (NARS), and supports the establishment of expert networks and best practices for genome editing. Through these efforts, the project seeks to enhance the efficiency of crop breeding programs, facilitate the responsible deployment of innovative technologies, and contribute to resilient and productive food systems in developing countries.

short_name: Panama-IDIAP-Asistencia Técnica para Productores Agropecuarios Pertenecientes a la Agricultura Familiar, Región 2. Provincia de Veraguas (Distritos: Calobre, San Francisco, Las Palmas, y Cañazas), Provincia de Los Santos (Distritos: Macaracas y Tonosí)
full_name: Panama-IDIAP-Asistencia Técnica para Productores Agropecuarios Pertenecientes a la Agricultura Familiar, Región 2. Provincia de Veraguas (Distritos: Calobre, San Francisco, Las Palmas, y Cañazas), Provincia de Los Santos (Distritos: Macaracas y Tonosí)
summary: This project supports the transition toward agroecological production systems among family farmers in Panama through participatory innovation, technical assistance, and capacity strengthening. The initiative promotes the adoption of sustainable agricultural practices by combining farmer-led experimentation, farm planning, innovation incentives, and collaborative research processes. Through engagement with producers, extension services, and local institutions, it strengthens the capacities required to implement and sustain agroecological approaches while fostering inclusive participation and knowledge exchange. The project contributes to improved resilience, productivity, and sustainability of farming systems and generates evidence on effective mechanisms for scaling agroecological innovations. By strengthening local innovation processes and institutional support systems, it helps create enabling conditions for broader uptake of sustainable agricultural practices.

short_name: GERMANY-GIZ-Supporting Soil Health Interventions in Ethiopia (SSHI – Phase III): Strengthening Data-Driven Agricultural Advisory Services and Soil Health Management for Smallholder Farmers
full_name: GERMANY-GIZ-Supporting Soil Health Interventions in Ethiopia (SSHI – Phase III): Strengthening Data-Driven Agricultural Advisory Services and Soil Health Management for Smallholder Farmers
summary: This project strengthens data-driven agricultural advisory services to improve soil health and productivity among smallholder farmers. The project integrates soil diagnostics, agronomic research, and digital decision-support tools to generate context-specific fertilizer and soil management recommendations. By enhancing national soil data systems and linking them with digital advisory platforms, SSHI Phase III supports evidence-based extension services that are responsive to local agroecological conditions. The project works closely with government institutions, research partners, and development actors to build capacity, harmonize soil health information, and scale sustainable land management practices. Ultimately, SSHI Phase III contributes to resilient farming systems, improved yields, and sustainable soil stewardship in Ethiopia.

short_name: GCDT (KFW) - Participatory Prioritization, Ecogeographic Gap Analysis, and Agri-Food Systems Analysis of Opportunity Crops in Support of PDFF Inception Phase
full_name: GCDT (KFW) - Participatory Prioritization, Ecogeographic Gap Analysis, and Agri-Food Systems Analysis of Opportunity Crops in Support of PDFF Inception Phase

short_name: WINDWARD FUND-Time2Graze: improving grazing management decisions of livestock systems in Tropical America project.
full_name: WINDWARD FUND-Time2Graze: improving grazing management decisions of livestock systems in Tropical America project.

short_name: BIUSA (SALL FAMILY) - 2025 Unrestricted Future Seeds Program and PABRA
full_name: BIUSA (SALL FAMILY) - 2025 Unrestricted Future Seeds Program and PABRA
summary: The project provides support to CIAT, on behalf of the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, for two strategic areas: the Future Seeds Program and the Pan Africa Bean Research Alliance (PABRA). The funding aims to advance charitable, educational, and scientific work aligned with the Alliance’s mission, including agricultural biodiversity conservation, seed systems, and inclusive agricultural development.
description: The system integrates satellite remote sensing, field observations, and predictive analytics to monitor water availability, identify drought hotspots, and generate actionable early warning information for government agencies, humanitarian organizations, and pastoralists. User-friendly information products are disseminated through web-based platforms and other accessible communication channels. The project will strengthen two key areas. First, it will provide core support to the Future Seeds Program by promoting the use of crop diversity in research, generating genomic knowledge for pre-breeding, and developing innovations for cassava seed systems. short_name: KOREA-KoLFACI-Research into the tolerance of common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) in Latin America, to confront climate change
full_name: KOREA-KoLFACI-Research into the tolerance of common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) in Latin America, to confront climate change
summary: This project aims to reduce drought-related losses in common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) production by developing and disseminating drought-tolerant varieties adapted to the needs of smallholder farmers in Latin America. Through collaboration among CIAT and national research programs in nine countries, the project combines plant breeding, field evaluation, seed dissemination, and capacity building. Key expected outcomes include the release of improved bean varieties with at least 20% higher yields under drought conditions, strengthened national breeding programs, enhanced regional research collaboration, and improved access to quality seed. The project ultimately seeks to increase agricultural resilience, sustain farmer livelihoods, and support food and nutritional security in the face of climate change.

short_name: JAPAN-MAFF-Development of Decarbonization Technologies for Livestock Systems in Adverse Environmental Conditions
full_name: JAPAN-MAFF-Development of Decarbonization Technologies for Livestock Systems in Adverse Environmental Conditions
summary: The Development of Decarbonization Technologies for Livestock Systems in Adverse Environmental Conditions project aims to create sustainable grazing management systems that reduce greenhouse gas emissions or increase carbon sequestration by up to 30% compared with conventional grazing practices. Implemented by CIAT with funding from the Government of Japan, the project focuses on using BNI forage grasses and multi-benefit forage legumes to improve livestock productivity, feed quality, soil health, and climate resilience. It will identify optimal forage-legume combinations, establish animal feeding and experimental plots, monitor cattle performance and soil carbon stocks, and use advanced tools such as C-mapper, remote sensing, and AI-based biomass estimation. The project also seeks to improve grazing rotation, increase forage biomass, and develop protocols for carbon credit generation under international standards

short_name: Reservas, FOIN y otras actividades propias de FLAR
full_name: Reservas, FOIN y otras actividades propias de FLAR
summary: This FLAR-related project supports core rice research coordination, regional collaboration, and strategic activities linked to the Latin American Fund for Irrigated Rice. Its activities are expected to strengthen rice research planning, partnership engagement, and the generation or consolidation of information useful for rice-based food security and regional research agendas. The project may contribute to CGIAR Science Programs where the work supports rice production, food security, scaling of research outputs, or partnership-based capacity sharing. Final mapping should be validated by the Rice Program scientific lead according to the specific activities financed under FLAR reserves, FOIN and related initiatives.

short_name: FAO (GEF) Scaling Information and Financial Services for Smallholder Adaptation (SIFSSA) - GCP/RAF/1070/LDF
full_name: FAO (GEF) Scaling Information and Financial Services for Smallholder Adaptation (SIFSSA) - GCP/RAF/1070/LDF
summary: The project project aims to increase the adaptive capacity of 50,000 smallholder farmers (60% women) in Uganda and Zambia by scaling digital information and financial services to mitigate climate-related risksThe initiative focuses on three core components: informing stakeholders through the effective use of farmer-generated data; designing bundled agro-advisory, insurance, and credit products tailored to specific risk profiles; and stimulating market supply and farmer uptake of Agricultural Risk Management (ARM) tools. By integrating climate-indexed insurance and risk-contingent credit, SIFSSA de-risks smallholder production, fostering long-term resilience and inclusive agricultural growth. This scalable model addresses critical barriers, such as poor data access and the lack of tailored financial instruments, by leveraging mass media and mobile platforms to deliver localized, gender-responsive solutions to vulnerable rural communities

short_name: Gates Foundation-Inception Phase for Breakthrough Bean and Cassava Products
full_name: Gates Foundation-Inception Phase for Breakthrough Bean and Cassava Products

full_name: UNEP -Waste to Wealth: Using innovative gender-responsive business models to turn organic market waste into organic fertilizer and animal feeds (WAWE)

It aims to transform organic market waste into valuable products, including organic fertilizers and protein-rich animal feed, through innovative and scalable circular economy business models in Kenya and Uganda, support use of the sustainably produced farm inputs by smallholder farmers and work with consumers to create/increase demand of the sustainably produced commodities. Expected outcomes include reduced methane and black carbon emissions from organic waste disposal, improved soil health through increased use of organic fertilizers, enhanced livestock productivity through affordable feed alternatives,  the creation of income-generating opportunities for women, youth, and waste-sector entrepreneurs and increasing consumption of sustainably produced commodities. The project will also strengthen knowledge, research, and investment in circular bioeconomy solutions, fostering sustainable urban food systems, climate resilience, and food and nutrition security across East Africa.

full_name: FFAR-Open Climate Resilience Platform for Global Adaptation ( IA Lead of A1792)

The project focuses on assessing climate risks for potato production and rice sourcing in Thailand, with projections extending to 2030. Through climate impact assessments, business risk quantification, and adaptation recommendations, the CRP will help farmers and businesses enhance resilience and promote sustainable agricultural practices. short_name: New Zealand-LIC-Technical support for Livestock Improvement Cooperation on a Livestock Information Vision for Ethiopia (aLIVE).
full_name: New Zealand-LIC-Technical support for Livestock Improvement Cooperation on a Livestock Information Vision for Ethiopia (aLIVE).
summary: This program aims to transform livestock data management and decision-making in Ethiopia by improving the availability, accessibility, quality, interoperability, and use of digital livestock data across the sector. The initiative supports the Ministry of Agriculture in consolidating fragmented livestock databases into a fit-for-purpose, scalable, cost-effective, and sustainable Livestock Information System that enables evidence-based planning, policy formulation, investment prioritization, and service delivery. short_name: IITA (AfDB) - Technologies for African Agricultural Transformation Phase II (TAAT II)
full_name: IITA (AfDB) - Technologies for African Agricultural Transformation Phase II (TAAT II)
summary: The Technologies for African Agricultural Transformation Phase II (TAAT II) project supports the scaling of high iron bean (HIB) technologies across Burundi, Cameroon, Kenya, Malawi, and Zimbabwe. Implemented by CIAT under an agreement with IITA and funded by the African Development Bank, the project aims to strengthen inclusive and sustainable seed systems, expand access to climate-resilient bean varieties, and promote the nutritional benefits of HIBs. Key activities include developing national value chain seed roadmaps, supporting early generation seed production, providing technical assistance to seed enterprises, organizing field days and outreach events, and strengthening agro-dealer networks for last-mile input delivery. The project also trains women and youth groups in seed business and processing of HIB products, while supporting innovation platforms that link value chain actors

short_name: RAAF-(Nigeria-ECOWAS)-Promote Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) in West Africa
full_name: RAAF-(Nigeria-ECOWAS)-Promote Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) in West Africa
summary: The purpose of this Agreement between RAAF/ECOWAS and CIAT is to define the modalities for the implementation of the activities of the Component No. 1 of the Regional Project to Promote Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) in West Africa: Improving knowledge and strengthening technical capacities, through regional and local interactions with the aim to promote agricultural practices that increase the are resiliences to the negative impacts of climate change.

short_name: Governors of St. Francis Xavier University - COADY (Comart Foundation) Accelerating Agroecology through ABCD: Personalized data outputs for evidence based farming
full_name: Governors of St. Francis Xavier University - COADY (Comart Foundation) Accelerating Agroecology through ABCD: Personalized data outputs for evidence based farming
summary: The "Accelerating Agroecology through ABCD" project is a targeted effort under the Alliance Bioversity-CIAT’s Multifunctional Landscapes Lever to implement agroecological food system transitions initially in Peru and Kenya, with plans to expand to other regions in subsequent years. This project aims to enhance the application of contextually relevant agroecological principles by addressing critical barriers faced by smallholder farmers, including inadequate financial literacy, unsustainable farming practices, and limited cooperative marketing efforts.

short_name: Solidaridad - Climate Heroes Project Asómbrate
full_name: Solidaridad - Climate Heroes Project Asómbrate
summary: The Asómbrate Project is a climate-smart agriculture and agroforestry initiative implemented by CIAT with financial support from Fundación Solidaridad Latinoamericana. The project aims to improve the productivity, sustainability, and climate resilience of 12,500 smallholder coffee and cocoa producers across the departments of Jinotega, Matagalpa, Boaco, Estelí, Madriz, and Nueva Segovia, Nicaragua. Implemented between May 2024 and December 2026, the project promotes the adoption of Climate-Smart Agricultural Practices (CSAPs) while supporting large-scale agroforestry restoration and carbon sequestration.
description: The Asombrate project seeks to create new economic opportunities for rural households by facilitating access to voluntary carbon markets through the ACORN platform. This innovative approach allows producers to potentially receive incentives linked to carbon sequestration generated by agroforestry systems. To support adoption, the project develops technical capacities through training programs, digital learning materials, farmer field schools, and the formation of rural promoters who can replicate knowledge within their communities.

short_name: BI (IFAD) - Private sector incentives and investments for climate change, resilience and environmental sustainability (Psii)
full_name: BI (IFAD) - Private sector incentives and investments for climate change, resilience and environmental sustainability (Psii)
summary: The PSii project focuses on developing innovative private and public sector incentive pathways for scaling agroecological practices to improve landscapes. Developing a better understanding and application for long-term incentives and transparent private sector engagement to support agroecological transitions for farmers and creating an enabling environment for scaling innovations. Key outcomes include: (1) Supported at least 100,000 households to engage with improved private and public sector incentive models and investments to adopt agroecological practices. (2) Improved the intergration of agroecological principles in transparent supply chains for rice, cocoa, and wheat value chains for at least 50,000 households. (3) Encreased the integration of agroecological metrics in supply chain transparency and traceability tools. (4) Improved policy enabling environment and existing business models for supporting agroecological transition for rice, cocoa and wheat value chains, and (5) Ehanced building local capacity, engaging multi-stakeholder platforms and co-mobilizing private sector investments to support agroecological transitions.
description: Both description and project summary filled. Transforming global food production systems, while also reducing their impact on the natural environment and improving welfare, remains a complex agenda characterized by overlapping trade-offs. Transitioning from ‚Äúbusiness as usual‚Äù requires simultaneous transformation across multiple levels ‚Äì from socioecological systems, economics, business, and politico-institutional systems ‚Äì to ensure the adoption of a more regenerative use of natural resources. However, too little attention is paid to the role of the private and public sectors in advancing to agroecological transition pathways. Although many business and private sector stakeholders are aligning to agroecological principles in food systems, there remains concerns among actors on the motivation, incentives, investments, and transparency of private sector initiatives. Under the TRANSITIONS program, the Private Sector Incentives and Investments (PSii) project will fill persistent knowledge gaps on the role of private and public sector incentives and investments in supporting agroecological transitions for farmers in low- and middle-income countries. The project will: (1) Review exisitng incentives mechanisms for supporting the promotion of agroecological practices, design incentive packages for scaling adoption of agroecological practices within agroecology smart landscapes for transitioning rice, wheat and cococa production systems, (2) Apply holistic metrics to digital traceability tools, and implement within at least one supply chain, (3) Improve enabling environment business models for supporting agroecological produced products, (4) Co-design and co-create incentive packages and building local capacity

short_name: Switzerland-SDC -Scaling Up Sustainable School Feeding Innovations in Rwanda (3SFI Project)
full_name: Switzerland-SDC -Scaling Up Sustainable School Feeding Innovations in Rwanda (3SFI Project)

The project aims to contribute to school feeding activities in Rwanda, supporting improved access to nutritious food for school-age children while strengthening related agricultural and food system activities.

short_name: SPAIN-AECID-Puesta en Marcha de la Acción NICACAO II
full_name: SPAIN-AECID-Puesta en Marcha de la Acción NICACAO II
summary: The NICACAO Project (Recovery of the Cocoa Value Chain in Nicaragua) is a initiative implemented by CIAT with financial support from the European Union and AECID to strengthen the sustainability, competitiveness, and climate resilience of Nicaragua’s cocoa sector. The project is being implemented between 2024 and 2026 in the department of Río San Juan, benefiting smallholder cocoa producers, producer organizations, women-led enterprises, and rural youth.
description: The NICACAO project focuses on three complementary components. First, it supports the rehabilitation and diversification of cocoa agroforestry systems through improved planting material, climate-smart agriculture, technical assistance, and sustainable production practices. Second, it strengthens post-harvest processing, quality management, circular economy approaches, and business development, with particular emphasis on women-led enterprises and youth participation. Third, it promotes traceability systems and compliance with emerging international standards, including European Union regulations on deforestation-free products and sustainable supply chains.

short_name: The University of Western Australia- (Australia -ACIAR)- Rapid breeding for reduced cooking time and enhanced nutritional quality in common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris)
full_name: The University of Western Australia- (Australia -ACIAR)- Rapid breeding for reduced cooking time and enhanced nutritional quality in common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris)

The agreement identifies Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, and Ethiopia as participating countries for project fund distribution. Through research collaboration, reporting, and shared project activities, the initiative seeks to support faster development and dissemination of improved bean materials.

full_name: UNITED KINGDOM-MET OFFICE-Enhancing Climate Change Resilience in East Africa (ECREA)
summary: Enhanced Climate Resilience in East Africa (ECREA), implemented in Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania, and Uganda under the WISER programme, strengthened the resilience of smallholder farmers by increasing access to localized and actionable weather and climate information services. The project enabled farmers to make climate-informed decisions that reduced losses, improved adoption of climate-smart practices, and generated more than USD 6 million in avoided losses. It also strengthened institutional collaboration among meteorological services, research organizations, extension systems, and local stakeholders, creating more responsive and trusted climate information systems. Socially, ECREA enhanced women’s participation in agricultural decision-making and demonstrated how integrated climate services can drive economic, social, and institutional transformation. The initiative provides a scalable model for building resilience while emphasizing the importance of greater youth engagement and locally tailored services.
description: Enhanced Climate Resilience in East Africa (ECREA), implemented in Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania, and Uganda under the WISER programme and led by the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT through PABRA, strengthened climate resilience among smallholder farmers by improving access to localized and actionable weather and climate information services (WCIS). Through partnerships with NMHSs, NARES, ICPAC, Agro-Advisory Committees (AACs), community radio, and digital platforms, the project established an innovative bundled agroclimate information model integrating forecasts, agronomic advisories, and local knowledge. ECREA achieved significant scale, directly training 326,561 farmers using the PICSA approach, establishing 17 AACs, and co-developing 24 customized WCIS products. Adoption and trust in climate services increased substantially, with notable improvements in extension-based delivery and WCIS uptake. The project demonstrated strong economic benefits, generating over USD 6 million in avoided losses through early warnings and climate-informed decisions. Socially, it enhanced women’s agricultural decision-making, particularly in Rwanda, and promoted climate-smart farming practices. ECREA provides a scalable model for resilience-building through economic, social, and institutional transformation, while highlighting the need to address youth engagement, accessibility, and localized forecast demand.

short_name: BIUSA (Bezos Earth Fund)-AI Grand Challenge Phase II: Rumen Digital Twin for Sustainable Livestock Production.
full_name: BIUSA (Bezos Earth Fund)-AI Grand Challenge Phase II: Rumen Digital Twin for Sustainable Livestock Production.
summary: The Rumen Digital Twin project aims to accelerate the development and deployment of enteric methane mitigation solutions through advanced artificial intelligence and data-driven modeling. The project will create a generative foundation model that captures the complex interactions among ruminants, their rumen microbiomes, diets, genetics, productivity, and methane emissions. By integrating large-scale multimodal datasets from global research collaborations, the model will generate realistic virtual cohorts of animals, enabling researchers and technology developers to explore how different interventions perform under varying biological and environmental conditions. Unlike conventional predictive models, the Rumen Digital Twin will provide a holistic representation of rumen function, allowing rapid simulation and optimization of methane-reducing strategies while reducing reliance on costly and time-consuming animal experiments. The project will also develop an open-access web platform and analytical tools to support researchers, livestock producers, feed and forage companies, breeding programs, and carbon market stakeholders in advancing climate-smart livestock systems.

description: The project is implementing an MRV system to track deforestation risks and emissions from livestock and agricultural activities. full_name: BMGF-Livestock water source monitoring and risk management system

Using satellite remote sensing, field observations, and predictive analytics, the system provides timely information on water availability and drought hotspots to support anticipatory action and informed decision-making. Designed for pastoral communities, including those with limited digital access and low literacy levels, it delivers accessible and actionable information through multiple communication channels. description:
This project strengthens Ethiopia’s drought-risk management by institutionalizing a near real-time livestock water and pasture monitoring and early warning system within the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) and the Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research (EIAR). Building on a livestock water monitoring system developed by the United States Geological Survey (USGS), the project adapts and scales the technology to support pastoral communities, particularly those with limited access to digital technologies and low literacy levels.
The system integrates satellite remote sensing, field observations, and predictive analytics to monitor water availability, identify drought hotspots, and generate actionable early warning information for government agencies, humanitarian organizations, and pastoralists. User-friendly information products are disseminated through web-based platforms and other accessible communication channels.
The project also delivers a gender-responsive capacity-building program involving government institutions, pastoral communities, NGOs, universities, and development partners. Through training, workshops, and continuous learning and feedback mechanisms, it strengthens the use of climate and water information for anticipatory action, drought preparedness, and sustainable livestock and pastoral resource management.

full_name: USA-USAID-Digital Fertility Mapping to Improve Agricultural Soil Management and Efficiency of Fertilization in Honduras
summary: Suelos de Honduras (https://suelosdehonduras.com) is a 3-year initiative (2023–2026) of the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT with Honduras' SAG-DICTA, addressing the country's fertilizer crisis through digital soil fertility mapping, evidence-based fertilizer recommendations, and Honduras' first AI-based soil information system. The project covers all 17 departments, has compiled over 5,400 soil samples, and works directly with nearly 479,000 farmers through the government's Bono Tecnológico Productivo program.
description:
Suelos de Honduras (https://suelosdehonduras.com) is a three-year project (2023–2026) led by the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT in partnership with Honduras' Secretariat of Agriculture and Livestock (SAG), the Science and Agricultural Technology directorate (DICTA), and the Bono Tecnológico Productivo (BTP), funded by USAID. The project responds to a structural crisis in Honduran agriculture: national soil data had not been updated since 1998, yet 90% of farmers rely on generic synthetic fertilizer formulas, and fertilizer import costs increased 137% in value in 2022 — meaning the country was fertilizing blindly and at growing expense.
The project operates through three interconnected objectives. First, it is producing the first high-resolution digital soil fertility map of Honduras, drawing on over 5,400 soil samples — both historical records and newly collected field data — across all 17 departments. Beta maps for soil pH and organic matter are already available, with a comprehensive multi-variable fertility map in progress. Second, it works with government institutions, the private sector, and farmer networks to improve fertilizer use efficiency: through the BTP alone, the project reaches 478,986 farmers who receive 575,000 bags of 12-24-12 formula and 230,000 bags of urea annually, and aims to ensure those inputs are applied based on actual soil conditions rather than generic prescriptions. Third, it has developed the Sistema de Información de Suelos, an AI-based decision-support platform that models crop yields under different soil, climate, and management scenarios for maize, beans, coffee, cassava, and plantain.
Beyond the technical products, the project catalyzed the formation of the Alianza Hondureña por el Suelo (AHS), a multi-stakeholder alliance bringing together SAG, FAO, DICTA, IHCAFE, Zamorano, and private sector actors around a shared soil health agenda. It also conducted soil characterization at DICTA experimental stations and established a standardized national soil sampling protocol (https://tinyurl.com/36d7dhbv). Due to the suspension of USAID funding, approximately USD 1.15 million in planned activities remain pending, including completion of the comprehensive fertility map and expansion of the modeling system to additional crops.

description:

Led by CIAT with support from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, the project focuses particularly on bean production in real farming conditions, including female-managed plots. Its purpose is to test whether selection directly under farmers’ environments can generate varieties that are more relevant, productive, and better adapted to the needs of smallholder farmers. By integrating genomic tools with on-farm evaluation, the project seeks to improve breeding efficiency and accelerate the development of bean varieties that perform well under diverse production conditions.

Its main objective is to facilitate farmers’ access to high-yielding hybrid rice technology through research, innovation, and collaboration with public and private partners. HIAAL works on the genetic improvement of parental lines and the development of hybrids with higher yield potential, disease tolerance, good milling quality, and culinary quality. The initiative also relies on a regional evaluation network across diverse agroecological zones in Latin America and the Caribbean, helping ensure that new materials respond to farmers’ needs and local production conditions. Overall, HIAAL seeks to improve the productivity, competitiveness, and sustainability of rice systems while contributing to food security and stronger agricultural innovation in the region.

In parallel, it will characterize sources of whitefly resistance and support their incorporation into breeding populations, contributing to reduced pest pressure and lower risk of CBSD transmission. summary: Artemis aims to transform breeding processes by leveraging AI and mobile phone technology to shift breeding programs from majority on-station to majority on-farm, alleviating critical logistical bottlenecks in phenotyping and shortening the breeding cycle. This is achieved through more efficient use of breeding technician time and provision of high quality and replicable data by enhancing the collection of reliable phenomic data through smartphones and to support breeder decision-making using on-farm collected data. A smartphone-deployable computer vision phenotyping tool makes phenotyping more efficient by reducing labor investment and overcoming limitations to the availability of highly trained technicians; reliability is increased as computer vision standardizes data collection and interpretation; and allows for the execution of on-farm breeding process as the phenotyping technology can be mobilized remotely. Computer vision leverages technology to collect data not possible by human eyes and it increases the amount, frequency and types of data, which can be used to derive novel breeding analytics expanding the data for decision making.

short_name: GATES FOUNDATION Developing novel methods to genetically improve common bean
full_name: GATES FOUNDATION Developing novel methods to genetically improve common bean
summary: The Developing Novel Methods to Genetically Improve Common Bean project aims to improve the climate resilience and productivity of common bean through modern breeding techniques. Led by the Centro Internacional de Agricultura Tropical (CIAT) with support from the Gates Foundation, the project focuses on developing and applying innovative genetic improvement methods that can accelerate the creation of better-performing bean varieties. These improved varieties are expected to help farmers respond more effectively to climate-related challenges while increasing productivity in bean-based food systems. The project contributes to agricultural research and development by supporting tools, knowledge, and breeding approaches that can benefit smallholder farmers and communities that depend on common bean as an important crop for food security and nutrition.
description:
This project aims to develop and validate a virus-induced Top-based genome editing platform for common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris), reducing the need for conventional plant transformation and regeneration while enabling efficient, heritable and transgene-free genome editing.

The technology will first be optimized in Arabidopsis and subsequently validated in selected common bean germplasm representing different market classes, including SEN56, SER323, DAA209, APm00009CIC, ARM00089CIC, AYW00079CIC, AYW00124CIC, MRD00168CIC, MBK00092CIC, among other Mesoamerican and Latin American bean varieties, depending on experimental validation and seed availability.

The project focuses on developing the genome editing platform rather than releasing new varieties. As proof of concept, target genes include reporter genes such as Phytoene Desaturase (PDS) to evaluate editing efficiency and heritability. Proposed traits will include abundant and deeper rooting, for example targeting the WEEP gene, photoperiod insensitivity, changes in determinacy, and will include learnings from the GEMINI project. Another key trait to be analyzed will be improved heat tolerance, drawing on the Rubisco activate thermal optimization proof of concept Gates investment (INV-058018). Further relevant traits to be considered include those related to yield, potentially focusing on identifying and manipulating 'anti-yield' genes to unlock greater productivity. Selection of traits will be a key determinant of the selection of germplasm used in future work.

The project is a collaboration between the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, UCLA, and UC Berkeley, combining expertise in bean breeding, viral delivery systems, and Top genome editing technologies to establish a broadly applicable genome editing platform for common bean improvement.
