summary:
The Business Acceleration for Youth Project (formally known as the Youth Business Acceleration and
Investment Facility) is a three-year (2021-2024), innovative initiative funded by USAID Malawi and led by the
Alliance of Bioversity International and International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT). Framed around
a resilience-led sustainability strategy, the project aims to strengthen the resilience of youth and women-led
business start-ups in Balaka, Chikwawa, Chiradzulu, Machinga, Mangochi, Mulanje, Thyolo, Nsanje and
Zomba, through the delivery of business incubation services creating growth-orientated, sustainable firms
able to secure and effectively utilize investment.
Nationally, the project is supporting Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) through the delivery of bespoke
technical support, industry specific expertise, mentorship and access to finance. The purpose of the project
is to accelerate and invest in youth-led enterprises that result in job creation, greater access to financing,
diversified incomes, a more inclusive private sector and improved household resilience in vulnerable districts.

short_name: BIUSA (Bezos Earth Fund)-Using genetic diversity to capture carbon through deep root systems in tropical soils  (Research and Capacity development)
full_name: BIUSA (Bezos Earth Fund)-Using genetic diversity to capture carbon through deep root systems in tropical soils  (Research and Capacity development)
summary: Carbon Sequestration project aims to use genetic diversity to capture carbon through deep root systems in tropical soils. The project focuses on tropical forages, rice, and rice–forage rotation systems, combining breeding, high-throughput phenotyping, gene editing, digital soil mapping, deep soil carbon measurement, and capacity building. Its objective is to develop deep-rooted plant materials that increase soil organic carbon storage while maintaining or improving productivity. Key outcomes include the evaluation of 45 forage grass genotypes and 37 rice genotypes, identification of promising deep-rooted rice donor lines, AI-powered root imaging tools, high-resolution soil carbon hotspot maps, and field evidence that rice–pasture rotations can increase root biomass by 49–56% and rice yield by 36%.

short_name: BMGF-Anti-methanogenic feedstock for livestock systems in global south
full_name: BMGF-Anti-methanogenic feedstock for livestock systems in global south
summary: The Low-Methane Forages (LMF) initiative is a CGIAR-led partnership involving ILRI, ICARDA, and the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, to develop and deploy AMC-rich forage-based solutions for reducing enteric methane emissions from livestock systems in the Global South. The project focuses on identifying, developing, and scaling high-yielding, nutritious, and drought tolerant forages (legumes and grasses) enriched with anti-methanogenic compounds (AMCs) that can reduce methane emissions while maintaining or improving animal productivity. Through a three-stage approach—discovery, development, and deployment—the project screens existing forages (both within and outside CGIAR genebank collections), validates promising candidates through in vitro and in vivo studies, and advances breeding and gene-editing strategies to enhance methane-reducing traits. In parallel, the initiative strengthens methane measurement infrastructure, improves emissions accounting, and creates enabling conditions for adoption, supporting climate-smart livestock systems, food security, and sustainable agricultural development across Latin America, Africa, and Asia.

summary: The Building Equitable Climate-Resilient African Bean and Insect Sectors (BRAINS) project aims to strengthen climate adaptation and inclusive economic development across bean, fruit tree, and insect value chains in 15 Sub-Saharan African countries. Implemented by CIAT in partnership with icipe, the project focuses on supporting smallholder farmers, women, youth, entrepreneurs, and value chain actors to adopt climate-smart agriculture technologies, nature-positive solutions, and sustainable business practices. It seeks to improve resilience to climate change, expand access to knowledge, finance, and innovation, and increase women’s and youth participation in leadership and climate governance. The project will directly reach at least 10 million people, including 60% women and girls, while indirectly benefiting around 50 million people through partnerships, platforms, farmer networks, and extension systems. Overall, BRAINS promotes low-carbon, climate-resilient food systems and more equitable opportunities in African agricultural economies.

description:
Description and project summary both filled. The "Screening, Developing, and Deploying Anti-Methanogenic Feedstock into Livestock Systems in the Global South" project aims to reduce methane (CH4) emissions from livestock, the single largest emitter in the agricultural sector, by leveraging the potential of novel compounds in CGIAR‚Äôs global collections of forages. This initiative involves screening, developing, and deploying anti-methanogenic feedstock into livestock systems in the Global South to achieve a significant reduction in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, equivalent to taking 7 million internal combustion engine cars off the road each year. Scope and Activities:
1. Discovery (WP1):
o Screen CGIAR gene bank collections to identify accessions with high levels of anti-methanogenic compounds (AMCs).
o Conduct metabolomics analyses to identify known and novel AMCs.
o Validate the anti-methanogenic activity of selected accessions through in vivo and in vitro assays.
2. Development (WP2):
o Promote the use of AMC-rich forage legumes directly in grazing systems.
o Enhance AMC levels in widely used forage-grass cultivars through conventional breeding and gene-editing techniques.
3. Deployment (WP3):
o Establish public-private partnerships for large-scale multi-environment feeding/grazing trials.
o Develop Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) systems for AMC-rich forages.
o Facilitate the adoption of AMC-rich forages in target regions.

full_name: Germany-BMWK-Supporting Colombia’s Just Energy Transition, climate resilience, and food security by introducing inclusive agri-photovoltaic systems JET-AgriSOL (IA Lead of A1794)
summary: The proposed project will support the Colombian Government in achieving its Just Energy Transition objective and NDC targets. By introducing and scaling APV systems, the project will contribute to promoting the energy-sovereignty and climate resilience of small-scale farmers, reducing GHG emissions, empowering women and youth to improve their livelihoods, and enhancing biodiversity. The project will set up micro- and medium-scale pilot and demonstration APV systems. Capacities for managing APV systems and combining them with climate smart agriculture will be strengthened by co-creating a vocational APV training program with Colombia¬¥s National Training Service. Inclusive, participatory and interdisciplinary research will be conducted on the pilot APV systems, and findings will be shared with a broad range of stakeholders. Further, context-specific and inclusive APV finance mechanisms will be co-designed, and public and private stakeholders supported to upgrade the enabling environment.
description: Description and project summary both filled. To support the Colombian Government in achieving its sustainable and Just Energy Transition goal, and meeting its agricultural and energy sectoral NDC targets through the nationwide expansion of photovoltaic capacity (impact), farmer communities have to co-develop and adopt inclusive and economically viable agri-photovoltaic (APV) solutions that can be further scaled through SDG-compliant public and private investments (outcome). This development will be initiated during the project‚Äôs first piloting phase, consisting of an APV pilot that will be installed on CIAT‚Äôs campus to carry out ‚Äúhigher-risk‚Äù research activities (output III). During the second piloting phase, lower-risk research activities will be conducted under real conditions on medium-scale APV pilots, on horticultural, arable, and pastoral land (output I). The diverse APV pilots form the basis for knowledge co-creation and serve for demonstration purposes, thereby promoting APV innovation-uptake and -scaling. Furthermore, women and men members of rural communities will be trained through a new praxis-oriented, and gender-responsive APV curriculum that will be developed and implemented with SENA‚Äôs (Colombia‚Äôs National Training Service) in-situ Rural Entrepreneurship (SER) program, focussing especially on developing capacities of disadvantaged groups (output II). This holistic skills development empowers rural community members to become more climate resilient and take advantage of new income opportunities. Finally, during the project‚Äôs third piloting phase, lessons learned from the experimental and medium-scale pilots will be integrated into the implementation of community-scale APV pilots, e.g., on the land of cacao producer organisations in PDET municipalities. Community-scale APV pilot will expand the green energy capacity of producer organisations and their communities, while promoting forest- and landscape-restoration activities (output I). The community-scale pilots play a key role in scaling APV systems and generating positive environmental impacts, while contributing to the energy-sovereignty of vulnerable rural communities. Moreover, inclusive and accessible APV-tailored financial mechanisms will be co-designed with local and international financial institutions (IFIs), further attracting investments to the APV sector, and enabling and encouraging small-scale farmers to adopt APV solutions (output IV). To further facilitate the inclusive adoption and scaling of APV systems, key binding constraints in the enabling environment will be identified and addressed through a multistakeholder process (output V).

description: CAL-PSE (Catalyzing and Learning through Private Sector Engagement for Biodiversity Conservation) is a strategic partnership originally established between USAID/Brazil and the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, operating in the Brazilian Legal Amazon. summary: The project “CteH 3 Modernizing Common Bean Improvement, from Gene Bank to Farmer’s Field” supports Crops to End Hunger by strengthening common bean breeding systems across Africa. Implemented by CIAT under a CIMMYT subgrant, it aims to modernize breeding infrastructure, increase genetic gain, and improve the delivery of productive, resilient, and market-preferred bean varieties. The project focuses on three African breeding hubs—Kawanda in Uganda, Chitedze in Malawi, and Selian in Tanzania—while also supporting Alliance capacity. Key activities include upgrading irrigation facilities, disease phenotyping platforms, parent-building platforms, pathology mini-labs, and high-throughput cooking-time assessment capacity. It also develops functional trait pipelines for climate resilience and insect resistance, reviews and adapts the OneCGIAR stage-gate system, and strengthens quality control, documentation, and genotyping of bean germplasm. short_name: WB-IDA-Development of Geospatial Methodologies to Prioritize NBS in the Rural, Agricultural and Forestry Sector
full_name: WB-IDA-Development of Geospatial Methodologies to Prioritize NBS in the Rural, Agricultural and Forestry Sector
summary: This project, commissioned by the World Bank's NBS Invest initiative (funded by GEF's Least Developed Countries Fund), develops a globally applicable geospatial methodology to identify and prioritize Nature-Based Solutions (NBS) in rural, agricultural, and forestry landscapes. The methodology supports decision-makers in LDCs and low-income countries to identify where NBS interventions—such as agroforestry, watershed restoration, sustainable land management, and silvopastoral systems—can deliver the greatest climate adaptation and mitigation benefits. The approach integrates biophysical, environmental, and socio-economic geospatial data layers to map NBS suitability across diverse country contexts. Outputs include a replicable methodology, documented data pipeline, and spatial tools to support World Bank project design and investment decisions, enabling greater mainstreaming of NBS into climate finance for smallholder and forest communities.
description:
Nature-Based Solutions are increasingly recognised as scalable interventions addressing climate, environmental, and socio-economic challenges in rural landscapes. However, authoritative, globally applicable geospatial approaches to identifying and prioritising NBS across multiple country contexts—particularly in Least Developed Countries—remain underdeveloped. This project addresses that gap through a World Bank-commissioned consultancy led by the NBS Invest Global Knowledge Platform.
The Alliance of Bioversity-CIAT leads the technical work, bringing expertise in geospatial analysis, remote sensing, climate modelling, and decision-support tool development. The methodology integrates multiple data layers—including climate hazards, land cover, biodiversity, topography, soils, and socio-economic conditions—to systematically identify areas where NBS interventions can deliver maximum adaptation and mitigation impact. The approach is designed to be replicable across diverse country contexts, with particular attention to data-scarce environments common in LDCs.
Sequential analytical steps include: identifying climatic risks and environmental pressures within defined spatial boundaries; assessing landscape suitability for specific NBS types; prioritising interventions based on climate benefit, co-benefits, and feasibility; and producing decision-ready spatial outputs for World Bank project teams and government counterparts. NBS types covered include agroforestry, watershed and forest restoration, sustainable land and water management, and silvopastoral systems.
Key outputs include a peer-reviewed geospatial methodology, a documented data pipeline, and spatial analytical tools made available as global public goods. The project directly supports the World Bank NBS Invest mission to increase planning and financing for NBS through World Bank projects, improve policy recognition, and strengthen country-level capacity to design and implement NBS initiatives in the agriculture and forestry sectors.

short_name: Windward Fund - Global Methane Hub Uncertainty Calculator for Tier 2 Cattle Methane
full_name: Windward Fund - Global Methane Hub Uncertainty Calculator for Tier 2 Cattle Methane
summary: This project supports the Global Methane Hub in developing and refining an uncertainty calculator for Tier 2 cattle methane emissions, aligned with IPCC 2006 guidelines. Accurate quantification of methane from livestock is critical for national GHG inventories and climate reporting under the Paris Agreement. Tier 2 methodologies require country-specific emissions factors and activity data, but calculating associated uncertainty ranges remains complex and inconsistently applied across national inventory teams. The project produces a validated, user-friendly tool that guides GHG inventory practitioners through uncertainty analysis for cattle enteric fermentation and manure management, following IPCC Good Practice Guidance. The calculator will improve accuracy and transparency in livestock methane reporting, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where livestock are a significant emissions source and capacity for uncertainty analysis is limited.
description:
National greenhouse gas inventories are required under the UNFCCC to report emissions from the livestock sector, with cattle enteric fermentation and manure management representing the dominant sources of agricultural methane in most countries. While the IPCC 2006 Guidelines provide a Tier 2 methodology for estimating cattle methane emissions using country-specific data and emissions factors, applying the associated uncertainty analysis correctly remains a significant challenge for national inventory teams, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where technical capacity is limited.
This project, funded by the Windward Fund through the Global Methane Hub, addresses this gap by developing a user-friendly, open-access uncertainty calculator tailored to Tier 2 cattle methane estimation. The tool guides inventory practitioners step-by-step through the propagation of uncertainty from input variables—including cattle population data, emissions factors for enteric fermentation and manure management, and activity data—following IPCC Good Practice Guidance on Monte Carlo simulation and error propagation approaches.
The calculator is designed to be accessible to non-specialist users while remaining technically rigorous, enabling national focal points and inventory compilers to produce uncertainty estimates that meet international reporting standards. It will be validated through collaboration with country-level inventory teams and peer review by Global Methane Hub technical experts. User documentation, a methodology report, and training materials will accompany the tool to support adoption and capacity building.
Key outcomes: (1) a validated open-access Tier 2 cattle methane uncertainty calculator; (2) a peer-reviewed methodology document; (3) training resources for national inventory teams; and (4) improved accuracy in cattle methane uncertainty reporting among target countries. The project contributes directly to improving the quality and transparency of livestock GHG inventories, supporting more effective climate policy under the Paris Agreement.

summary: The Amazon Biodiversity Fund (ABF) Brazil is a $ 50 million private market impact fund tackling the financing gap for sustainable businesses in the Brazilian Legal Amazon. Co-designed by USAID and the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, the fund deploys long-term venture capital across four key pillars: landscape conservation, sustainable agroforestry (such as cocoa and açaí), smallholder value chains, and green technology. By its 2030 target, ABF aims to directly conserve 650,000 hectares of high-biodiversity forest, protect critical endangered species, and restore degraded lands. On the climate front, it is built to avoid 3.9 million tons of $CO_2$ emissions. Structurally focused on socio-economic impact, the fund integrates over 2,000 Indigenous people and local smallholders into sustainable markets, legally guaranteeing that up to 70% of project-generated revenues flow back to these local communities to secure long-term livelihoods.

description: This project supports the World Bank in translating agricultural carbon crediting concepts into practical guidance for project design and implementation. The work focuses on identifying the technical, institutional, financial, and MRV conditions required for successful Results-Based Climate Finance (RBCF) and Voluntary Carbon Market (VCM) initiatives in agriculture. Through case studies, operational lessons, and decision-support tools, the project helps Task Team Leaders assess readiness, prioritize investments, and understand trade-offs associated with carbon finance. Particular attention is given to soil carbon, agricultural practices, MRV systems, additionality, farmer participation, and scaling pathways that can support climate and development objectives simultaneously.
